TheGovernmentofBotswana(GoB) is undertaking the Promoting Participation and Enhancing Learning (PROPEL) (P513800) project supported by the World Bank (WB).  

The Project Development Objective (PDO) is to increase participation in preprimary and senior secondary education and improve learning conditions in supported schools, particularly at the junior secondary level. The Project consists of the following four components: 

  • Component 1: Increasing participation in education 
  • Component 2: Enhancing the learning environment 
  • Component 3: Strengthening system capacity for quality education service delivery 
  • Component 4: Project management and implementation support 

 

The Ministry of Child Welfare and Basic Education (MCWBE) is the implementing entity for the Project. AProject Delivery Unit (PDU)(or Program Coordinating Unit) is being  establishedwithin MCWBE to support the effective implementation of project activities, including procurement and contract administration; monitoring, evaluation and reporting of progress under the project; fiduciary management; and environmental and social safeguards management. Specifically, the PDU will be responsible for preparing the Project Operations Manual (POM) to guide the implementation of the project. The MCWBE seeks to engage an Individual Consultant to support the preparation of the POM.

 

The objective of this assignment is to support the PDU in the development and finalization of the POM to clearly describe how the project will be implemented to achieve the expected development objectives and outcomes.

 

The POM is expected to be the key document which describes the structure of the project and the many stakeholders that are going to be involved in its implementation, including defining the roles and responsibilities of the various stakeholders under each component and sub-component and clarifying the implementation arrangements for all the components and sub-components.

 

The POM should include (i) detailed description of Project activities; (ii) the specific roles and responsibilities of the Project Steering Committee (PSC), PDU, and other entities participating in the implementation of the project and the arrangements for ensuring coordination among them; (iii) arrangements on fiduciary matters, including financial management, audit, and procurement; (iv) institutional administration coordination and day to day execution of project activities; (v) selection criteria and modalities for technical assistance in project supported activities; (vi) monitoring and evaluation; (vii) reporting arrangements; (viii) social and environmental safeguards requirements and procedures; and (ix) other technical and organizational arrangements and procedures as shall be required for the Project.

 

The POM will be organized or structured as follows:

 

  • Section 1 will describe the Project Context. This will include a brief background to the development of the project; state the Project Development Objective (PDO) and the indicators that will be used to measure progress towards the achievement of the objective; clarify the project target beneficiaries; and define the scope of the project.
  • Section 2 will discuss implementation arrangements by components, sub-components and activities of the project. It will include detailed implementation plan (IP) for each activity under the sub-components with clear selection criteria for specific activities. This will also include a detailed section on implementation modalities for activities related to civil-works and community driven development.
  • Section 3 will describe the institutional administrative and implementation arrangements of the project by entity-roles, attributions and responsibilities.

  • Section 7 will discuss social and environmental safeguards requirements and procedures.
  • Section 8 will discuss Grievance Redress Mechanisms, (GRM), Citizen’s Engagement, Gender and Climate actions.

  • Section 10 will discuss training and capacity building plan under the project.

  • Outline of the Project Operations Manual.

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): EG-EEAA-559382-CS-QCBS

The Greater Cairo Air Pollution Management and Climate Change Project (herein “the Project”) aims at reducing air emissions from critical sectors and increasing resilience to air pollution in Greater Cairo. The Project aims more specifically at reducing air emissions which is a key step toward the reduction of pollution concentrations and improvement of air quality. The Project will focus on two of the primary sources of air pollution in the Greater Cairo (GC) region (i.e., Cairo, Giza and Qalyoubia Governorates): open burning of solid waste and vehicle emissions; and will include six main components aiming at: (i) enhancing the air quality management framework and decision support system in Egypt; (ii) improving Solid Waste Management services; (iii) reducing air and climate pollutants from vehicle emissions; (iv) furthering stakeholder engagement, awareness and communication; (v) project management and monitoring & evaluation (M&E); (vi) addressing the important issue of unintended emissions of POPs.

Brief description about the  Enhanced E-Waste and HCW management for Reduction of uPOPs:                 

 It is an additional finance (AF) to the parent project; this new activity focuses on reduction of unintended persistent organic pollutants (uPOPs) aligns with the “GEF Project Design and Review Considerations in Response to the COVID-19 Crisis and the Mitigation of Future Pandemics”. This new component will comprise 3 sub-components.

Sub-component 6.2: Supporting Effective Healthcare Waste Management, Models, and Solutions has been designed under the proposed Greater Cairo Air Pollution Management and Climate Change project (P172548).

This sub-component aims to strengthen the enabling environment for sustainable healthcare waste (HCW) management. It seeks to develop and pilot innovative solutions to reduce unintentional Persistent Organic Pollutants (uPOPs) emissions and promote long-term systemic changes in HCW practices across Egypt.

Key activities under this sub-component include:

(i)         developing and modeling public/private financing and investment models for collection and treatment of HCW.

(ii)        providing technical assistance to select healthcare institutions on utilization of possible financial mechanisms, procurement of environmentally-sound equipment, training of staff, and integration with the new protocols and facilities.

(iii)       supporting the preparation of a plan to roll out proper HCW management throughout the country in collaboration with key agencies and stakeholders (including women and other vulnerable communities).

(iv)       pilot appropriate recycling and re-sale of safely segregated HCW.

The requested services covered by these terms of reference are to support the Project Coordination Unit (PCU) and the Technical Implementation Units (TIUs) of “Greater Cairo Air Pollution Management and Climate Change (GGAP&CC) Project” in the implementation of the service of Developing Guidelines for the Healthcare Waste Management in Egypt

2. Review Existing Legal Guidelines

  • Review and update the existing HCWM guidelines developed under the GEF Medical and E-waste Project (2018), incorporating legislative and institutional updates, including the roles and responsibilities of all relevant authorities and stakeholders (WMRA, EEAA, MOHP, MOHE, EDA) involved in healthcare waste management. Identify gaps and areas requiring updates based on current regulations and practices.

3. Stakeholder Engagement

  • Collect and consolidate requirements, standards, and procedures from key entities such as WMRA, EEAA, MOHP, EDA, Ministry of higher education (MOHE), and other relevant stakeholders.
  • Organize consultations and workshops with stakeholders to gather feedback and ensure alignment.

4. Review HCW audit report conducted for the Ain Shams Specialized and French Kasr elany hospitals conducted within project.

  • The consultant should review and take into consideration the findings of the healthcare waste audit report conducted in this project at the two hospitals under study.

5. Update Existing Guidelines

  • Draft comprehensive HCWM guidelines incorporating:
    • National regulations and policies.
    • Input from stakeholders.
  • Address all stages of HCWM, including generation, identification, segregation, storage, transportation, treatment, and disposal.

6. Validation and Finalization

  • Circulate the draft guidelines to stakeholders (WMRA, EEAA, MOHP, MOHE, EDA) for validation and feedback.
  • Revise and finalize the guidelines based on received input.
  • Organize a workshop with all stakeholders to present the final version.

  • A detailed work plan outlining the timeline for the proposed tasks.
  • Report on the review of existing guidelines and identified gaps.
  • Stakeholder consultation report summarizing collected inputs and feedback.
  • Draft  healthcare waste management guideline for adoption by the Ministry of Local development and Environment in coordination with the relevant competent authorities. Submit a concise "Key Issues and Resolution Report" outlining:

 (i) the main gaps and inconsistencies identified in the existing HCWM guidelines and how they have been addressed in the updated draft; and

The Southern African Development Community (SADC) is a Regional Economic Community comprising of 16 Member States, namely, Angola, Botswana, Comoros, Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), Eswatini, Lesotho, Madagascar, Malawi, Mauritius, Mozambique, Namibia, Seychelles, South Africa, Tanzania, Zambia, and Zimbabwe. Established in 1992, SADC is committed to regional integration and poverty eradication within Southern Africa through economic development and ensuring peace and security.

Guided by the Regional Indicative Strategic Development Plan (RISDP) 2020-2030, and premised upon the SADC Vision 2050, the SADC Region has developed the Implementation Plan for the Regional Indicative Strategy Development Plan, for regional integration that seeks to promote cooperation amongst Member States for macro-economic beneficiation. One of the strategic objectives of the RISDP is to facilitate improved disaster risk management in support of regional resilience.

In view of the above, the SADC Secretariat is undertaking a number of interventions aimed at increasing the resilience of the SADC economies, improvement of livelihoods of the region’s communities and the protection and restoration of biodiversity and the region’s ecosystems. One such initiative is the Regional Climate Resilience Program (RCRP), which is a programmatic framework (structured as a series of projects or SOPs), funded by the World Bank, with the objective of strengthening the resilience to water-related climate hazards and their impacts in Eastern and Southern African countries.

The Project Development Objective (PDO) of the RCRP-1 RCRP project is to improve the management of water-related climate impacts in Eastern and Southern Africa.

One of the key priorities within the SADC Region is strengthening regional and national Multi-Hazard Early Warning Systems (MHEWS). Under Component 1, the project supports operationalization of the SADC Humanitarian and Emergency Operations Centre (SHOC), national early warning capacity assessments, interoperability between national systems, SHOC and the African Multi-Hazard Early Warning and Early Action System (AMHEWAS), and implementation of recommendations from the SADC Regional Ministerial Conference on Early Warning Systems. The consultancy contributes to the United Nations Early Warnings for All (EW4All) Initiative.

In order to realise the intended outcome SADC seeks to undertake this activity through the recruitment of an individual consultant. The consultancy adopts a Regional Coordination–National Implementation model. The SADC Secretariat will coordinate the process regionally and provide quality assurance while working closely with the international EW4All Pillar Lead Agencies: UNDRR (Pillar 1), WMO (Pillar 2), ITU (Pillar 3) and IFRC (Pillar 4). notice_text:
Hirshabelle State of Somalia

Ministry of Interior and Local Government.

BULSHO PROJECT - Strengthening Community Institutions for Social Cohesion, Inclusion and Resilience.

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (REOI)

 

Individual Selection of Consultant

Country: Federal Government of Somalia

Project ID No. P508408

Name of the Project: Bulsho Project - Strengthening Community Institutions for Social Cohesion, Inclusion and Resilience

Consulting Service: PIU Bulsho PFM Specialist   

Individual/Firm: Individual

Ref No: SO-MOIFAR-571563-CS-INDV

Duty Station: Jowhar, Hirshabelle Somalia (with potential travel to the target Districts and Cities of Bulsho Project)

 

Deadline: 7th November, 2026

 

BACKGROUND OF THE PROJECT

 

The Bulsho Project – Strengthening Community Institutions for Social Cohesion, Inclusion and Resilience (P508408) is under the lead of the Ministry of Interior, Federal Affairs and Reconciliation – MoIFAR of the Federal Government of Somalia and responsible for the national program called Bulsho, the Somali word for society. The Bulsho Program puts citizens and communities at the center of the government’s action.  The Bulsho Program is a Somali government-led initiative designed to strengthen community and local institutions, fostering social cohesion, inclusion, and resilience. As Somalia continues its recovery from two decades of civil war, the program places a strong emphasis on enhancing service delivery, rebuilding the social contract, and promoting community-centered governance. This uniquely Somali-owned and -driven initiative underscores government ownership and leadership at federal, member state, and district levels, ensuring institutional sustainability and the realization of key policy outcomes.

The Ministry of Interior and Local Government of Hirshabelle State of Somalia have established Project Implementation Units - PIUs, headed a State Project Managers, which have the responsibility for the activities that take place in Hirshabelle State.

The PIUs are responsible for managing project activities at state-level and to liaise with districts. Specifically, the PIUs are responsible for: (i) Verifying eligibility of districts, appraising districts’ request to participate – this includes allocation of Bulsho packages and conducting lottery for each package and verifying the fulfilment of district commitments. (ii) Preparing state-level procurement plans. (iii) Preparing annual project work plans and budgets for state-level activities. (iv) Carrying out procurement for state-level activities. (v) Managing the contract with the logistic firm. (vi) Delivering capacity building activities and providing quality assurance and technical backstopping to districts - this includes trainings of district officials and staff. as well as community entities that play a role in the project. (vii) Preparing requisitions for funds to be transferred to districts, as per the project workplan, and in accordance with the grant agreement/sub-agreements and this POM and its annexes. (viii) Preparing quarterly narrative and financial reports for project activities taking place in their states. (ix) Verifying technical and E&S appraisal of local investments (Component 3) as well as other E&S actions as per the Environment and Social Management Plan. (x) Verifying the soundness of sustainability plans for the local investment prepared by the districts, including Operations & Maintenance (O&M) plans and the Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs) for the management of local infrastructures; and (xi) Preparing security management plans and applying security protocols in partnership with the security firm.

The Ministry of Interior of Hirshabelle State of Somalia is seeking to use a portion of the Bulsho Project to finance the recruitment of a Public Financial Management – PFM Specialist to support the Hirshabelle Project Implementation Unit - PIU.

Responsibilities: For the Bulsho Project activities, the PFM Specialist will work in closely with the PCU Financial Management and Procurement Specialists for oversight, guidance, quality assurance and also to ensure harmonization of procedures, and compliance with fiduciary requirements. The role will also provide technical support and capacity building to cities and district counterparts. The PFM Specialist in collaboration with the Hirshabelle State External Assistance Fiduciary Section (EAFS), prepare Unaudited Quarterly Financial Reports (IFRs) and Annual Financial Statements, ensuring adherence to international reporting standards.

The PFM Specialist is to ensure that Bulsho Financial Management and Procurement are done in line with the applicable Somalia Government and World Bank procedures and second is to support build Public Financial Management (PFM) capacity at the FMS, Districts and Community levels. The PIU Public Financial Management (PFM) Specialist will be required to be an all-around PFM professional combining both financial management and procurement responsibilities.

The State PIU PFM Specialist will perform the following key areas: -

A. Financial Management

  1. Financial Reporting and Oversight: Prepare and submit periodic financial reports (monthly, quarterly, annually) in approved formats, ensuring compliance with the financing agreement and also ensure timely identification and reporting of material variances for financial oversight and strategic decision-making and also ensure internal audit is carried out by Ministry of Finance (MoF) on project activities.
  2. Budgeting and Financial Planning: Develop and review annual work plans for the PIU and consolidated Bulsho budget in collaboration with PIU and the District Focal Points (DFPs), ensuring alignment with the standard chart of accounts. The budget to be consolidated by the MoIFAR and approved by Parliament by December 31and also prepare, monitor, and interpret cash flow forecasts to support financial planning and ensure disbursements align with approved budgets, work plans, and financial agreements.
  3. Fund Disbursement and Payment Processing: Verify payments adhere to accounting practices and financing agreements, obtaining No Objection letters through PCU where applicable and also facilitate the district disbursement requests through the Hirshabelle State EAFS and the Hirshabelle MoF and disburses the funds to the District Approved Accounts (DAAs).
  4. Subledger Reconciliation and Documentation: Conduct monthly bank reconciliations for the project accounts and also prepare Statements of Expenditure (SoEs) to ensure accurate financial tracking and timely documentation in client connection and ensure timely and regular updates to the Fixed Assets Register, conducting physical verification of assets at least twice a year and ensure regular update the Contracts Disbursement Register, ensuring proper reconciliation of new contracts and supplier payments.
  5. Audit Coordination and Risk Management: Work with auditors to facilitate timely annual financial audit and address queries and ensure compliance with internal control systems, EAFS manual, POM, COAPM, and other regulatory procedures and identify emerging fiduciary risks that inform revisions of the EAFS manual and POM, including Matching Grants Manual (MGM).
  6. Regulatory Compliance and Updates: Keep abreast of changes in financial regulations and ensure accounting staff remain updated and ensure no project category or component is overspent without proper World Bank authorization.

B. Procurement

1. Procurement Planning: Under the guidance of the PIU Project Manager, in consultation with the other PIU specialists, and in and close collaboration with the PCU Procurement Specialist, prepare the annual procurement plans for Hirshabelle State Bulsho activities and update the overall procurement plan for the state, in line with the consolidated national procurement plan and budget for Bulsho and track the implementation of the Hirshabelle State Procurement Plan, by updating progress against the Procurement Plan’s milestones, providing details on challenges and remaining actions, and indicating when procurement activities have been completed.

2. Tender Processing: Prepare inputs such as Terms of Reference, Schedules of Requirements, Specifications, Prequalification Documents (PQDs), Bidding Documents (BDs), and Requests for Proposals (RFPs), in line with World Bank regulations, the Bulsho POM and the project procurement plan and manage all procurement processes, including preparation and issuance of invitations, receipt of proposals and bids, opening of EOIs, proposals, and bids, evaluation of submissions, and preparation of evaluation reports in line with World Bank regulations and the Bulsho POM.

3. Contract Management: Under the direct guidance of the Project Manager, manage all contracts awarded under the project, including monitoring execution, tracking deliverables, and ensuring timely delivery of goods, services, and consultant reports in full compliance with contractual provisions and under the direct guidance of the Project Manager, address procurement-related queries, disputes, and complaints, and ensure issues are resolved in accordance with World Bank regulations, the Bulsho POM and applicable procedures.

4.  Compliance and Reporting: Ensure that all procurement activities comply with applicable World Bank regulations, the Bulsho POM and Government procedures, and submit reports to the PIU Project Manager and PCU Procurement Specialist for oversight and also together with the technical specialists, carry out direct verification of all purchased goods, services and works, by verifying that purchased goods, services and works are timely delivered and meet the specifications indicated in the purchase orders or contracts.

C. Capacity Building

  1. Conduct financial management and procurement training needs assessments and prepare structured capacity-building plans for the PIU, district finance officers and community committees implementing Bulsho-funded local investments, in coordination with the Local Government Institute (LGI).
  2. Provide tailored, hands-on mentoring and on-the-job support to district governments and community committees in procurement and contract management, focusing on the practical application of Bulsho project rules and procedures.
  3. Support districts and community committees in carrying out their procurement functions, including preparation of tender documents, evaluation of bids, contract award and management, and oversight of the procurement cycle, in compliance with the Bulsho POM and World Bank regulations.
  4. Participate in joint reviews, training sessions, and learning events organized by the PCU, and cascade knowledge to PIU and district staff.

D. Monitoring, Evaluation, and Reporting:

  1. The PFM Specialist shall collaborate with the PIU M&E Specialist to ensure that financial and procurement data are integrated into the project’s results framework.
  2. Track progress against fiduciary indicators (e.g., disbursement rate, audit completion, compliance score) and also contribute to quarterly performance reviews and fiduciary compliance summaries shared with MoIFAR, FGS and the World Bank.

 

Selection Criteria: The selection shall be based on qualification, experience and skills of the candidate and followed by an interview. The qualifications, experience and competencies include:

  1. Educational Background
  • Bachelor’s degree in accounting, finance or business administration.
  • Professional qualification in financial management, registered by and attained final qualification of any financial management related recognized professional body e.g. CIPFA IPFM, ACCA, CPA etc.
  •  Procurement training will be an advantage.

    2. Professional Experience

  • Minimum of 7 years of relevant experience in financial management including broad expertise in the public or private sector.
  • At least 5 years’ experience implementing financial management and procurement actions under international development partner guidelines (e.g., World Bank, African Development Bank, United Nations).
  • Experience in project financial management in developing countries; experience in fragile or conflict-affected environments is highly desirable.

    3. Skills and competencies

  • Familiarity with computerized accounting systems (e.g., ERP systems such as PASTEL, QuickBooks) and proficiency in accounting/procurement software.
  • Demonstrated knowledge of World Bank financial management and procurement procedures.

      4. Knowledge

  • In-depth knowledge of Somalia’s public financial management laws and regulations.
  • Knowledge of Somalia's Government Procurement policies and regulations or knowledge of WB and/or development partner procurement related standards and requirements

     5. Language skills/requirement.

  • Excellent command of both English and Somali (reading, writing, and presenting) is essential.

REPORTING

The PFM Specialist will report to the Hirshabelle Bulsho PIU Project Manager. For technical oversight and quality assurance, the Specialist will maintain direct reporting lines to the PCU Financial Management Specialist and the Procurement Specialist.

TIMING Duration of Assignment:

The PFM Specialist shall be contracted for up to 12 months with 3 months of probationary period) and renewable upon satisfactory performance.

The Ministry of Interior and Local Government of Hirshabelle State of Somalia now invites eligible Individual Consultants to indicate their interest in providing the above-mentioned services. Interested consultants must provide the following (i) Curriculum Vitae (CV) with 3 reference persons; (ii) copies of certificates of academic qualifications; and (iii) cover letter indicating that they are qualified to perform the services.

SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to section III, para 3.14,3.16 & 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Projects Financing Goods, Works, Non -Consulting and Consulting Services, July 2016, revised November 2017, August 2018, November 2020 and September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.  

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations. 

Interested candidates should submit their applications, including a detailed updated CV and cover letter, outlining their experience and qualifications in relation to the role marked with the subject title of the position by the following email address: recruitment.moihss@outlook.com   and copy to procurement@bulsho.moifar.gov.so  latest by 7th November, 2026 at 04:00 PM Mogadishu time.

notice_text:
The Government of Botswana is undertaking the Promoting Participation and Enhancing Learning (PROPEL) (P513800) project supported by the World Bank.

 

The Project Development Objective (PDO) is to increase participation in preprimary and senior secondary education and improve learning conditions in supported schools, particularly at the junior secondary level. The Project consists of the following four components:

  • Component 1: Increasing participation in education
  • Component 2: Enhancing the learning environment
  • Component 3: Strengthening system capacity for quality education service delivery 
  • Component 4: Project management and implementation support

 

The Ministry of Child Welfare and Basic Education (MCWBE) is the implementing entity for the Project. A Project Delivery Unit (PDU) (or Program Coordinating Unit) is being established within MCWBE to support the effective implementation of project activities, including procurement and contract administration; monitoring, evaluation and reporting of progress under the project; fiduciary management; and environmental and social safeguards management. Specifically, the PDU will be responsible for ensuring that implementation of social risk management activities is conducted in an efficient, transparent, and compliant manner. To strengthen implementation capacity and support timely delivery, the MCWBE seeks to engage an Individual Social Development Consultant as a core member of the PDU.

 

The objective of this assignment is to ensure that project activities comply with relevant national regulatory requirements as well as the World Bank's Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) and applicable Environmental and Social Standards (ESSs). This includes identifying and mitigating potential social risks, instrument preparation, monitoring, and reporting, overseeing stakeholder engagement and grievance redress processes, and building the capacity of MCWBE to manage social issues effectively throughout project implementation.

 

The Social Development Consultant will perform duties that include, but are not limited to, the following:

  • Social Risk Management: (i) Support PDU in establishing social risk management systems, screening tools, and procedures in line with Project Environmental and Social Commitment Plan (ESCP) requirements, including contributions to the Project Operations Manual (POM); (ii) lead or support the preparation of E&S instruments required under the ESCP and oversee fulfillment of ESF commitments, review site-specific Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP), conduct field visits, and maintain supervision records; and (iii) ensure E&S requirements (ESMP, LMP, Code of Conduct) are reflected in bidding documents and contracts prior to issuance; review contractor-submitted E&S plans and verify implementation on site. 
  • Gender Based Violence (GBV) and SEA/SH (Sexual Exploitation and Abuse and Sexual Harassment): Work closely with the GBV Specialist on the development and implementation of the SEA/SH Action Plan, and its integration into project activities.
  • Stakeholder Engagement: Implement the Stakeholder Engagement Plan (SEP), lead consultations with stakeholders including communities, schools, and government partners, and ensure inclusion of vulnerable groups.
  • Grievance Redress Mechanism: Facilitate establishment and operation of an accessible GRM, with appropriate channels to receive SEA/SH complaints, monitor resolution of complaints, and ensure confidential handling of SEA/SH cases, including adequate dissemination of information regarding GRM reporting channels to stakeholders and affected communities.
  • Labor and Working Conditions: Monitor contractor compliance with Labor Management Procedures (LMP) under ESS2.
  • Monitoring, Reporting, and Capacity Building: Prepare quarterly monitoring reports, contribute to mid-term and final evaluations, and strengthen capacity for MCWBE staff, school administrators, and project partners on E&S requirements. Develop guidance notes, checklists, and practical tools to support social risk management of the project.
  • Perform any other related tasks assigned by the supervisor within the scope of the assignment.

 

The Social Development Consultant will work as an integral member of the PDU and report to the Project Coordinator. The Social Development Consultant will work in close day-to-day coordination with the Environmental Consultant, GBV Consultant and other PDU staff and will maintain regular communication with the MCWBE and the World Bank Social Specialist assigned to the project.

 

The duration of the assignment is an initial period of 2 years from contract signature with a probationary period of three (3) months. A formal performance evaluation shall be conducted at the end of the first twelve (12) months by the MCWBE evaluation committee. Continuation of the contract for the second year shall be subject to a satisfactory performance assessment and availability of project funding. The performance assessment will consider, among other factors, the quality and timeliness of deliverables, compliance with the Terms of Reference, and overall effectiveness in supporting project implementation. After the initial period of 2 years, the contract will be renewable for the duration of the project based on satisfactory performance and project needs. The Ministry of Child Welfare and Basic Education now invites eligible individual consultants to indicate their interest in providing the services. Interested consultants must provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services.

 

The Social Development Consultant shall have the following minimum qualifications:

  • Master's degree in social sciences, sociology, anthropology, social work, gender studies, development studies, human geography or another relevant discipline.
  • Advanced training or specialization in areas such as social risk management, stakeholder engagement; training in gender and social inclusion will be an added advantage.
  • At least 5 years of relevant professional experience in social development, social safeguards, or related fields in the context of development projects.
  • Proven experience with infrastructure projects, with education sector experience being highly desirable.
  • Demonstrated experience with social sustainability issues in education sector or infrastructure projects, including gender mainstreaming, GBV prevention and response, inclusion of vulnerable groups, stakeholder engagement, and community grievance redress mechanisms.
  • Experience implementing and monitoring social risk management instruments (Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP), Stakeholder Engagement Plan (SEP), Resettlement Action Plan (RAP), Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM)) in projects financed by the World Bank or other international financial institutions.
  • Solid understanding of the Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) and Environmental and Social Standards (ESSs).
  • Experience working in Botswana or the Southern Africa sub-region is strongly desirable.
  • Familiarity with Botswana's national legislation on social protection, gender, labor, and child welfare is an advantage.
  • Ability and willingness to undertake regular field travel.
  • Strong analytical, communication, and report-writing skills in English and Setswana.
  • Excellent interpersonal and facilitation skills, with demonstrated ability to engage diverse stakeholders including government officials, school communities, civil society, and vulnerable groups.
  • Computer literacy, including proficiency in standard office software and data management tools.

 

The position offers competitive remuneration for the selected individual.

The attention of interested consultants is drawn to Section 111, paragraphs 3.14,3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IFP Borrowers (February 2025 version), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

The selection will be made in accordance with the “World Bank Procurement Regulations for Investment Project Financing Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services” (July 2016) revised in November 2017, August 2018, November 2020 & September 2025.

Candidates who meet the required qualifications will be assessed based on the following evaluation criteria. The first ranked candidate will be invited for contract negotiations.

  • Notify his/her supervisor and the World Bank of any serious environmental, OHS, or CHS incident; participate in investigations and prepare corrective action plans per ESCP timelines.
  • Prepare and submit quarterly E&S monitoring reports and provide environmental inputs to World Bank supervision missions and implementation status reports.
  • Support implementation of the Stakeholder Engagement Plan (SEP) on environmental matters, facilitate community consultations at project sites, and ensure timely in-country disclosure of all cleared E&S instruments.

  • Prepare timely annual and quarterly disbursement forecasts for all components of the Project in line with the Project’s procurement plan.

REPUBLIC OF ANGOLA

MINISTRY OF SOCIAL ACTION, FAMILY AND THE ADVANCEMENT OF WOMEN

PROJECT TO STRENGTHEN THE SOCIAL PROTECTION SYSTEM FOR HUMAN CAPITAL AND RESILIENCE

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS)

Consultancy Services: Assessment and Specification of Equipment Required for the Single Social Registry (CSU)

Reference No.: SCEXT-SER 06-2025

The Republic of Angola, through the Ministry of Social Action, Family and the Advancement of Women (MASFAMU), has received financing from the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD), under Loan No. IBRD-97180, to support the implementation of the Project to Strengthen the Social Protection System for Human Capital and Resilience (P181495). The Project Implementation Unit (UIP-CSU) intends to apply part of the proceeds of this financing to eligible payments under the contract for the consultancy services described in this notice.

The assignment will include, inter alia: (i) assessing and surveying the CSU’s equipment requirements; (ii) evaluating alternatives available on the market; (iii) analysing suitability, performance, safety, interoperability, sustainability and cost-effectiveness; (iv) preparing neutral, clear and measurable technical specifications; (v) defining requirements for installation, technical support, maintenance and warranty; and (vi) preparing a technical matrix and recommendations to inform future procurement. The detailed scope and deliverables are set out in the Terms of Reference (ToR).

The UIP-CSU invites eligible consulting firms to express their interest in providing the services. Interested firms shall provide information demonstrating that they possess the qualifications and relevant experience required to perform the assignment, including experience in assignments of a similar nature and complexity. At the Expression of Interest stage, the assessment will focus on the firm’s qualifications and experience; Key Experts will not be evaluated at this stage.

The assessment will consider, among other relevant factors: (i) experience in assessing, planning and specifying technological equipment and infrastructure; (ii) experience in information-systems integration and related solutions; and (iii) knowledge of information security, interoperability, support and maintenance requirements, and cost analysis. Experience in public-sector and/or social-protection projects will be considered relevant.

The consulting firm will be selected using the Quality- and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method, with an open international market approach, through a lump-sum contract. The procurement is financed 100% from the proceeds of Loan No. IBRD-97180 and is subject to post review by the World Bank. República Dominicana

No. de Referencia: DO-MAP-546062-CS-QCBS

 

Estimados señores:

 

El Gobierno de la República Dominicana ha recibido financiamiento del Banco Mundial para cubrir el costo del Proyecto de Apoyo a la Implementación del Plan de Reforma y Modernización del Estado, a través del Ministerio de Administración Pública (MAP), y tiene la intención de aplicar parte de los fondos para la contratación de servicios de consultoría.

Los servicios de consultoría ("los Servicios") comprenden el diseño, desarrollo y apoyo a la implementación de la Arquitectura Empresarial de la Administración Pública, aplicando una metodología compatible con los marcos PAERA/GovStack, o con marcos equivalentes compatibles con el enfoque de Infraestructura Pública Digital (DPI). Incluyen el diagnóstico de la situación actual (AS-IS) y la definición del estado objetivo (TO-BE); su traducción en una Arquitectura de Soluciones basada en componentes reutilizables (building blocks), patrones, estándares abiertos y blueprints; el diseño de la capa de interoperabilidad y de la infraestructura digital compartida del Estado; el modelo de gobernanza de la arquitectura; un roadmap de implementación por fases con la ejecución de al menos dos (2) pilotos; y el diseño e implementación de un Modelo de Gestión de Datos Holístico que permita el uso estratégico, seguro y eficiente de los datos a nivel gubernamental, acompañado de un programa de transferencia de conocimiento y fortalecimiento de capacidades. La consultoría tendrá una duración estimada de doce (12) meses, contados a partir de la firma del contrato. Esta descripción es de carácter general; el detalle de los alcances, productos y especificaciones técnicas se encuentra en los Términos de Referencia (TDR) que se anexan a la presente Solicitud de Expresiones de Interés (SEI).

El Ministerio de Administración Pública (MAP), a través de la Unidad Implementadora del Proyecto (UIP), invita a las firmas consultoras elegibles ("Consultores") a expresar su interés en proporcionar los Servicios. Los Consultores interesados deben proporcionar información que demuestre que tienen las calificaciones requeridas y la experiencia relevante para prestar los Servicios. Los criterios para la selección de la lista corta son los siguientes:

  1. Constitución y trayectoria: firma legalmente constituida, con al menos cinco (5) años de operación.
  2. Experiencia demostrable. en al menos dos (2) proyectos durante los últimos siete (7) años relacionados con arquitectura empresarial/de gobierno/pública digital, transformación digital del sector público, interoperabilidad gubernamental, gobernanza y gestión de datos, arquitectura pública digital o servicios públicos digitales.
  3. Al menos un (1) proyecto en los últimos cinco (5) años que haya involucrado arquitectura empresarial/de referencia del sector público o multiinstitucional, definición TO-BE, interoperabilidad o intercambio de datos, gobernanza/institucionalización, hoja de ruta por fases y transferencia de capacidades.
  4. Conocimiento o experiencia aplicable en PAERA/GovStack, TOGAF, ArchiMate, estándares abiertos, building blocks, interoperabilidad y capacidades comunes.
  5. Experiencia demostrable en el diseño o implementación de arreglos de gobierno digital, arquitectura empresarial o gobernanza tecnológica del sector público, incluyendo roles institucionales, mecanismos de decisión, estándares, procesos de revisión o capacidades de arquitectura/gobernanza.

Adicionalmente, se valorará la experiencia en transformación digital a escala nacional o del sector público; América Latina y el Caribe; organismos multilaterales; infraestructura pública digital. GovStack, PAERA, DPI Safeguards, X-Road, OpenG2P, OpenFN, credenciales verificables o equivalentes. Racionalización de aplicaciones, plataformas compartidas o capacidades comunes. Diseño e implementación de modelos de arquitectura, gobierno digital o gobernanza tecnológica, o unidades de arquitectura, más allá de la experiencia mínima requerida. Arquitectura de servicios públicos centrada en las personas. Gestión de datos públicos, interoperabilidad semántica y fuentes autoritativas.

Nota: Los expertos clave no serán evaluados en esta etapa.

Para estos fines se requiere que los Consultores interesados remitan la siguiente documentación:

  • Carta de expresión de interés, con los datos generales de la firma (firmada y sellada por el representante legal).
  • Detalle de la experiencia de la firma donde se evidencie la actividad principal, los años en el negocio, la experiencia relevante y la capacidad técnica y de gestión, conforme a los criterios de preselección indicados. Para cada proyecto referido se deberá indicar: cliente, país, período de ejecución, rol de la firma (líder, socio o subconsultor), principales entregables y datos de contacto del cliente.
  • Estructura organizativa de la firma, con una breve descripción del personal técnico disponible para la prestación de los Servicios.
  • Registro mercantil actualizado o documentación equivalente que acredite la personería jurídica vigente y la fecha de constitución de la firma.
  • Documentación de respaldo de la experiencia presentada: contratos, actas de recepción, informes aprobados, constancias de conformidad, certificaciones, órdenes de servicio, cartas del cliente, enlaces públicos verificables u otros medios equivalentes razonables.

CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR THE DESIGN REVIEW AND CONSTRUCTION SUPERVISION OF BANSARA IRRIGATION SCHEME, CROSS RIVER STATE

Phase I – Design Review: Reviewing, updating, and validating the existing detailed engineering designs, hydraulic modelling, structural calculations, technical specifications and cost estimates for the irrigation infrastructure (headworks, canal networks, drainage systems, and access roads and expansion of the scheme).

Phase II – Construction Supervision: Acting as the Engineer representative / Supervisor to oversee civil works, ensuring compliance with approved designs, technical specifications, safety standards, quality assurance, timeframes.

The State Project Implementation Unit (SPIU) now invites eligible consulting firms ("Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The shortlisting criteria are:

  • Core business as an engineering consulting firm with at least 10 years of general experience in water resources and irrigation infrastructure development.
  • Proven track record of executing at least Two (2) similar assignments involving design and or construction supervision of medium-to-large scale gravity/pressurized irrigation schemes in sub-Saharan Africa or similar contexts within the last 8 years.
  • Technical and organizational capability of the firm (provide structural overview, quality control certifications, and managerial structure).

 (Note: Key Experts’ CVs are not evaluated at this REOI stage).

The Organisation of Eastern Caribbean States (OECS) Commission has received funding from the World Bank toward the cost of the OECS Data for Decision Making (DDM) Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for Consultancy For Building Capacity and Compilation of Gender Equality Indicators in OECS Data for Decision Making (DDM) Project Beneficiary Countries- Grenada, St Lucia and St Vincent and the Grenadines.

 

The goal is to strengthen the evidence base on gender equality in OECS Member States, monitor progress in reducing gender gaps, and inform public policy and decision-making.”

  1. ABOUT THE OECS

The Organisation of Eastern Caribbean States (OECS) is an International Inter-governmental Organisation dedicated to regional integration in the Eastern Caribbean.  Its vision for 2020-2024 is "A better quality of life for the people of the OECS". Its mission is: "To drive and support sustainable development through regional integration, collective action and development cooperation". The OECS came into being on June 18th, 1981, when seven Eastern Caribbean countries signed a treaty agreeing to cooperate and promote unity and solidarity among the Members. The Treaty became known as the Treaty of Basseterre, named in honour of the capital city of St. Kitts and Nevis where it was signed.

 

  1. PROJECT BACKGROUND

 

The Organization of Eastern Caribbean States is implementing a regional statistical capacity building project, financed by the World Bank Group, with Grenada, Saint Lucia, and Saint Vincent and the Grenadines (Participating Countries). The OECS Data for Decision Making (DDM) Project (called “Project” going forth) comprises five components that will be implemented over a five-year period. At the national level, Component 1 and Component 2 of the Project will strengthen national statistical systems through (i) statistical modernization and capacity building, and (ii) data production, analysis, and dissemination, with a focus on the population and housing census, living conditions surveys, labor market surveys, and agricultural census. At the regional level, Component 3 of the Project will support the OECS Commission’s mandate for regional integration and the strengthening of the regional statistical system. Component 4 will support project implementation, and Component 5 will provide a contingency option for immediate surge funding in the event of a national emergency. The OECS Commission will be responsible for the implementation of Component 3. The Project aims to improve the capacity of participating countries to produce and publicly disseminate statistical data for country and regional level analytics, which will enable greater data-driven decision making at both the national and regional levels.

 

For additional information, see the Project Appraisal Document (Report No:  PAD4314) (http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/520151651261033077/Grenada-Saint-Lucia-Saint-Vincent-and-the-Grenadines-Organization-of-Eastern-Caribbean-States-Commission-OECS-Data-for-Decision-Making-Project) and Financing Agreement (http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/099540006172231884/P174986080af360d20a39f013f5cdf84a18)

 

 

 

 

  1. INTRODUCTION

 

The realization of the 2030 Agenda and the commitment to “leave no one behind” requires

the disaggregation of a wide array of gender and SDG indicators that measure inequalities and address the needs of women and men, boys and girls in the Caribbean. It also necessitates the strengthening of capacity to generate these indicators and statistics. The CARICOM Gender Equality Indicators (GEI) framework was developed in collaboration with UN Women and Members States and aimed to enhance CARICOM Member States’ capacity to monitor and assess their progress in meeting gender equality goals and targets including the SDGs. The CARICOM GEI was based on a comprehensive review of the Global UN Minimum Set of Gender Indicators developed and ratified in 2013 and revised in 2021. It comprises forty-eight (48)quantitative and eleven (11) qualitative indicators. These indicators were validated at the 40th Meeting of the Standing Committee of Caribbean Statisticians in 2015 and have subsequently been updated.

 

While OECS MS have agreed to compile this list of GEI Indicators only one country Dominica has produced a report on these indicators while St Lucia conducted a gender data management assessment in 2019 to identify the challenges faced by the government in producing gender statistics. This Consultancy seeks to build on previous work done in the compilation of gender indicators and statistics in the Caribbean using the GEI framework as the base for further capacity building and measuring and collecting information on issues relevant for gender equality and women's empowerment.

The indicators are organised into five (5) themes: Economic empowerment; Education; Health and related services; Public life and decision-making; and Human rights of women and girl children

 

  1. GOALS AND OBJECTIVES OF THE REPORT

 

The goal is to strengthen the evidence base on gender equality in OECS Member States, monitor progress in reducing gender gaps, and inform public policy and decision-making.”

 

Objectives

  1. To generate robust, evidence-based statistics and indicators on gender equality for St Lucia, Grenada, and St Vincent and the Grenadines to inform policy formulation and planning.
  2. To build capacity among MS in the compilation, collection, validation, analysis, and dissemination of quantitative gender indicators and statistics compiled primarily from the Population and Housing Census (PHC).
  3. To widen accessibility and availability of gender indicators and statistics and to enhance the quality of this information and to promote their effective use by researchers, policymakers, service providers, planners, and the general public.

 

To achieve the objectives of the Consultancy, the report will compile gender equality indicators and statistics in the following domains:

 

  • Economic Activity and Empowerment
  • Education
  • Human Rights of Women and Girls
  • Health and Related Services
  • Public Life and Decision Making

 

 

  1. SCOPE OF SERVICES AND OUTPUTS

The consultant will perform the following services and produce the following outputs remotely:

  1. Review of CARICOM GEI List and revised UN Minimum List and update the CARICOM GEI List where applicable
  2. Develop a detailed inception report covering the analytical approach, workplan, tabulation plan, list of indicators, harmonisation methodology, and timelines
  3. Produce three sex disaggregated draft and final statistical country profiles (one per country) summarising all CARICOM Gender Equality and SDG Indicators that can be derived primarily from the PHC. To the extent that data are available from other sources such as the Survey of Living Conditions (SLC), Labour Force Surveys (LFS) and Agricultural Censuses from all three countries these can also be used.

 

  1. Produce visuals e.g. infographics, charts, graphs etc. on the key dimensions for highlighting
  2. Produce a Step-by-Step Manual on the compilation of GEI Indicators in all MS
  3. Attend and present draft findings at review meetings with the OECS Regional Data Governance Council (RDGC) Secretariat.
  4. Plan, coordinate and facilitate a virtual/face to face capacity building workshop on the compilation of the CARICOM GEI in collaboration with OECSC and the host country
  5. Produce a final report and associated outputs incorporating feedback from the RDGC and the RDGC Secretariat.
  6. Produce Power Point presentation, as well as visuals and messages for infographics and social media and dissemination activities on gender equality statistics
  7. Engagements and meetings with key MS Stakeholders.

 

  1. DURATION

 

The assignment is expected to be undertaken over a six (6) month period.

The Organisation of Eastern Caribbean States (OECS) Commission has received funding from the World Bank toward the cost of the OECS Data for Decision Making (DDM) Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for Consultancy Services to Implement Communications Plan for the OECS Regional Data Governance Council (RDGC) and the Data for Decision Making (DDM) Project.

The Terms of Reference for this consultancy and EOI template are provided below.

 

 

       

 

                                  

 

 

 

 

OECS DATA FOR DECISION MAKING (DDM) PROJECT

 

 

 

Consultancy Services to Implement Communications Plan for the OECS Regional Data Governance Council (RDGC) and the Data for Decision Making (DDM) Project

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

  1. About the OECS

The Organisation of Eastern Caribbean States (OECS) is an International Inter-governmental Organisation dedicated to regional integration in the Eastern Caribbean.  Its vision for 2020-2024 is "A better quality of life for the people of the OECS". Its mission is: "To drive and support sustainable development through regional integration, collective action and development cooperation". The OECS came into being on June 18th, 1981, when seven Eastern Caribbean countries signed a treaty agreeing to cooperate and promote unity and solidarity among the Members. The Treaty became known as the Treaty of Basseterre, named in honour of the capital city of St. Kitts and Nevis where it was signed.

  1. PROJECT BACKGORUND

The Organisation of Eastern Caribbean States is implementing a regional statistical capacity building project, financed by the World Bank Group, with Grenada, Saint Lucia, and Saint Vincent and the Grenadines (Participating Countries). The OECS Data for Decision Making (DDM) Project (called “Project” going forward) comprises five components that will be implemented over a five-year period. At the national level, Component 1 and Component 2 of the Project will strengthen national statistical systems through (i) statistical modernisation and capacity building, and (ii) data production, analysis, and dissemination, with a focus on the population and housing census, living conditions surveys, labour market surveys, and agricultural census. At the regional level, Component 3 of the Project will support the OECS Commission’s mandate for regional integration and the strengthening of the regional statistical system. Component 4 will support project implementation, and Component 5 will provide a contingency option for immediate surge funding in the event of a national emergency. The OECS Commission will be responsible for the implementation of Component 3. The Project aims to improve the capacity of participating countries to produce and publicly disseminate statistical data for country and regional level analytics, which will enable greater data-driven decision making at both the national and regional levels.

 

For additional information, see the Project Appraisal Document (Report No:  PAD4314) (http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/520151651261033077/Grenada-Saint-Lucia-Saint-Vincent-and-the-Grenadines-Organization-of-Eastern-Caribbean-States-Commission-OECS-Data-for-Decision-Making-Project) and Financing Agreement (http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/099540006172231884/P174986080af360d20a39f013f5cdf84a18).

 

 

 

 

  1. GOALS AND OBJECTIVES

3.1 Goal

To support the Data for Decision Making (DDM) and Regional Data Governance Council (RDGC)  in the rollout of a suite of marketing, communications and event planning activities for initiatives being pursued in relation to the DDM project and RDGC.  This consultancy will lead the Implementation of the RDGC Communications Strategy to increase visibility, stakeholder engagement, trust in official statistics, and uptake of RDGC outputs across OECS Member States and development partners Specifically, the Communication Specialist will support the visibility and dissemination of key DDM Project outputs, including guidance notes and regional thematic reports. The consultant will also assist the participating DDM countries in developing and implementing dissemination plans to promote the reach and use of surveys conducted under the Project. A comprehensive list of the expected outputs is provided in Annex 1.

In addition, the consultant will be responsible for designing and implementing a beneficiary satisfaction survey covering the outputs disseminated under the Project, particularly those resulting from the Population and Housing Census data collected under the Project, as well as analysing the findings to assess the effectiveness of dissemination efforts and inform strategies for enhancing the visibility, reach and impact of the Project’s output

3.2 Objective

The objective of the consultancy is to develop and implement a fully expressed Public Relations and Communications Campaign aimed at supporting the use of data produced by national statistical offices. This is to enhance the visibility, accessibility and use of data produced under the DDM Project for country-level and regional analytics, by strengthening data dissemination, stimulating demand for data, and promoting its use in decision-making. This is intended to create a reinforcing cycle in which increased data use drives greater demand for data, encouraging sustained data production and further use.

  1. SOPE OF WORK

 

    1. General Activity

The consultant will work closely with the OECS Communications Unit, relevant technical units and subject-matter specialists within the Commission, as well as designated staff of the Central Statistical Offices (CSOs) in the direct beneficiary countries, to develop and implement a coordinated communications campaign. The campaign will include targeted activities to enhance visibility, accessibility and use of the data and other outputs generated through the Project.

    1. Specific Activities

 

      1. Support the development and implementation of country-level dissemination plans. Work with the Central Statistical Offices (CSOs) and relevant stakeholders in the participating DDM countries to develop and implement dissemination plans for key statistical operations and outputs, including the Saint Lucia Household Budget Survey (SLHBS), Agricultural Census, Labour Force Surveys, Population and Housing Census, and national thematic reports produced under the Project.

 

      1. Support the launch and promotion of national statistical outputs. Assist participating countries in planning and executing launch events and related communication activities for surveys and the publication of national thematic reports, ensuring that findings are effectively communicated to policymakers, development partners, the media and the wider public.

 

 

      1. Develop and implement a regional communications strategy. Design and coordinate a regional communications strategy to enhance the visibility, accessibility and use of outputs produced under the regional component of the DDM Project, including the OECS Microdata Catalog, guidance notes and regional thematic reports.

 

      1. Develop engaging, multi-format communications materials. Produce and coordinate the development of audience-appropriate communications materials to promote both regional and national DDM outputs. These should include infographics tailored to different social media platforms, short videos, audio recordings, graphics, key messages, media content and other audiovisual products that highlight the value and practical applications of the statistical outputs. Assignment: Consultancy Services for Data Processing, Statistical Analysis and Report Preparation for the Saint Lucia Survey of Living Conditions and Household Budget Survey (SLC-HBS) and OECS Harmonised Labour Force Survey (HLFS)

The Government of Saint Lucia has received World Bank financing for the OECS Data for Decision Making Project and intends to use part of this financing for the consulting services described below. The Ministry of Economic Development and Youth Economy, through its Project Implementation Unit, invites eligible consulting firms to submit expressions of interest.

Assignment scope

The firm will support the Central Statistical Office (CSO) and the Ministry of Equity, Social Justice and Empowerment in processing, validating and analysing survey data, preparing dissemination-ready statistical reports and strengthening counterpart capacity. The services comprise:

  • Data processing and quality assurance: Review survey instruments, methodologies and classifications; clean, edit, impute and validate data; assess completeness and consistency; and produce metadata, documented procedures and reproducible analytical files.
  • Poverty and living conditions analysis: Construct a consumption-based welfare aggregate; estimate monetary poverty and inequality using approved poverty lines; develop a Multidimensional Poverty Index using the Alkire-Foster methodology; analyse household welfare and access to services; and compare findings with 2016 estimates where feasible.
  • Consumer Price Index (CPI) modernisation: Review the current compilation framework; map household expenditure to COICOP 2018; derive and update expenditure weights; develop the updated CPI framework and calculation tools; test and link the new and existing series; and prepare an implementation roadmap.
  • Labour market analysis: Analyse two available quarters of the OECS Harmonised Labour Force Survey (HLFS) using International Labour Organization (ILO) and applicable International Conference of Labour Statisticians (ICLS) standards; produce labour market indicators; assess comparability with the existing survey and potential breaks in time series; and provide linking guidance where applicable.
  • Reporting and knowledge transfer: Prepare draft and final poverty, CPI and HLFS products; present findings for stakeholder validation; develop dissemination materials and website-ready indicators; and provide training and documented knowledge transfer.

 

Principal outputs include an inception report, data quality assessments, cleaned and validated datasets and technical documentation, HBS-CPI mapping and weighting files, report outlines, CPI testing and linking results, final poverty and HLFS reports, an updated CPI framework and implementation roadmap, and a capacity-building report.

Duration: Seven (7) months from contract signature. Tentative commencement: December 2026. The firm will work under the Director of Statistics or designate for the HBS and HLFS, and the Ministry of Equity technical lead for the SLC. The detailed TOR accompanies this notice.

Firm qualifications and shortlisting criteria

Interested firms must demonstrate the following qualifications and experience, as specified in the TOR:

  • At least ten (10) years of experience in official statistics, survey analysis, census data processing or related fields.
  • Proven expertise in household survey analysis, labour force surveys, agricultural statistics and census data through at least two (2) similar assignments.
  • Successful completion of at least two (2) assignments of comparable scope and complexity for national statistical offices, international organisations, development partners or public sector institutions.
  • Experience preparing official statistical publications, analytical reports and dissemination products.
  • Technical capacity using R, Stata, SPSS, SAS, CSPro, SQL or equivalent statistical and data processing tools, supported by adequate managerial and quality assurance arrangements.
  • Experience delivering training, capacity building and knowledge transfer.
  • Experience in Small Island Developing States, the Caribbean or comparable developing-country contexts will be an asset.

Shortlisting will assess the firm’s qualifications and experience. Individual Key Experts will be assessed at the proposal stage rather than during shortlisting. The TOR identifies a Team Leader / Senior Statistician, Labour Market Statistics Specialist, Poverty Statistician and Consumer Price Statistician.

Submit a signed expression of interest in English, a firm profile describing its core business and years of operation, and details of relevant completed assignments. Objective and scope of the assignment

The consultancy will support the Central Statistical Office (CSO) in reviewing and validating the 2022 Enterprise Census data, conducting statistical analysis, and preparing a comprehensive analytical report. The report will describe Saint Lucia’s business sector, identify policy-relevant findings and, where comparability permits, examine changes since the 2009 Enterprise Census.

The Consultant will undertake the following principal activities:

  • Review the census methodology, metadata and microdata; assess data quality and work with CSO staff to resolve or document issues; develop an analytical framework, report outline and detailed tabulation and analysis plan.
  • Analyse enterprise characteristics, economic activity, industry, size, ownership, geographic distribution and employment, including employment by sex; produce thematic tables and cross-tabulations using the final dataset approved by the CSO.
  • Use relevant official statistical and administrative sources where appropriate, documenting differences in coverage, concepts, reference periods and classifications.
  • Prepare statistical tables, charts, maps and other visualisations in accordance with CSO publication standards; draft the analytical report with findings, policy implications and recommendations.
  • Present preliminary findings, support technical and stakeholder validation, address agreed comments, and deliver the final report, presentations, analytical outputs and technical documentation, including reproducible syntax or code.

Duration and working arrangements

The assignment is for five (5) months, with a tentative commencement in December 2026. It may be undertaken primarily remotely, with virtual and/or face-to-face meetings, technical sessions, presentations and consultations as required. The Consultant will work under the overall supervision of the Director of the CSO and in collaboration with the designated technical focal point and subject-matter specialists.

The Consultant must comply with applicable statistical confidentiality, data protection and CSO security requirements, including any required oath of secrecy or confidentiality undertaking.

Inception report and analytical work plan within two weeks; data review, validation and tabulation plan by month 1; preliminary tables and visualisations by month 2; draft analytical report by month 3; stakeholder presentation and validation during month 4; and final analytical report and data and technical documentation package by month 5.   • Demonstrated experience analysing large statistical datasets, preferably business surveys, enterprise or economic censuses, or establishment surveys.
  • Demonstrated experience preparing analytical reports using census or survey microdata.
  • Knowledge of statistical concepts, methodologies and internationally recognised standards for official statistics.
  • Proficiency in statistical software such as R, Stata, SPSS, CSPro, Python or equivalent packages.
  • Experience producing statistical tables, charts, graphs and other data visualisations.
  • Experience analysing data using the International Standard Industrial Classification of All Economic Activities (ISIC), preferably Revision 4.

Name of Project

Just Transition in Select Coal Regions of Bosnia and Herzegovina

Loan No.

IBRD-98010

Assignment Title

Consultancy service for Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) for Raspotoje Mine Closure

Procurement Plan Ref Number

BA-FBIH-JCT-CS-CQS-26-2.2.7

Country of Delivery

Bosnia and Herzegovina

The Federal Ministry of Energy, Mining and Industry (FMERI) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Just Transition in Select Coal Regions of Bosnia and Herzegovina Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for the following consulting services.

Federal Ministry of Energy, Mining and Industry (FMERI)  is seeking to appoint a consultancy company to support the Federal Ministry of Energy, Mining and Industry (FMERI), Zenica coal mine (RMU Zenica) and the utility company Elektroprivreda BiH (EPBiH) in closing the underground mine Raspotoje. This consultancy supports the comprehensive Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) and a corresponding Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP) for Raspotoje underground coal mine. The services are expected to start at December 2026 and to be finalized until the end of May 2027.  

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website: https://fmeri.gov.ba/project-implementation-unit/

The Federal Ministry of Energy, Mining and Industry (FMERI) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers [dated September 2023] (“the Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

The best qualified firm to carry out the services will be selected in accordance with the Consultant’s Qualifications Based Selection (CQS) method set out in the Regulations and based on the following criteria:

  1. Core business and years in business 30%;
  2. Qualifications in the field of the assignment 60%;
  3. Technical and managerial organization of the firm and availability of key staff within the firm 10%;

CVs of Key Experts will not be evaluated in evaluation of expressions of interest.

MINISTRY OF MINERALS AND ENERGY

 

PROJECTS AND ENERGY DEVELOPMENT UNIT (PEDU)

 

Invitation for Expression of Interest

 

Consulting Services- Firms Selection

 

Geotechnical Studies for a Wind Farm in Botswana

 

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for Geotechnical Studies for a Wind Farm Site

Reference: EOI/MME-PEDU/002/26-27

 

  1. BACKGROUND

 

Botswana plans to harness its renewable energy (RE) resources and accelerate renewable energy development through the implementation of the Integrated Resource Plan (IRP). The Government of Botswana is currently developing renewable energy projects at several pre-selected sites. The Project and Energy Development Unit (PEDU) under the Ministry of Minerals and Energy (the Client) is responsible for the development of these projects. A feasibility consultant has identified a proposed site for a wind farm based on a multi-criteria assessment considering preliminary wind resource data, transmission infrastructure, land use and ownership, and preliminary environmental and social considerations.

 

The geotechnical studies will support the development of a proposed 100 MW wind farm located north of Letlhakane, Botswana. The final coordinates and boundaries of the area to be investigated will be confirmed by the Client prior to commencement of the assignment.

 

  1. SCOPE OF WORK

 

The Client is seeking a qualified and experienced consulting firm to undertake geotechnical investigations to support the pre-development of the proposed 100 MW wind farm.

 

The assignment will include preliminary site-wide geotechnical investigations and, subsequently, location-specific investigations based on the preliminary wind farm layout.

 

The detailed scope, investigation areas, technical requirements and deliverables will be set out in the Terms of Reference provided at the next stage of the selection process.

 

  1. QUALIFICATIONS

 

PEDU invites eligible consulting firms ("Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the services. Interested consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services. The shortlisting criteria are:

  1. Core Business: Minimum of ten (10) years of experience undertaking geotechnical investigations and related studies.
  2. Demonstrated experience in satisfactorily completing geotechnical investigations for utility-scale energy or comparable infrastructure projects.
  3. Demonstrated experience in undertaking geotechnical investigations for at least minimum two (2) utility scale projects in Sub- Saharan Africa.
  4. The Consultant to demonstrate  experience in undertaking comparable assignments in accordance with applicable technical, environmental and occupational health and safety standards
  5. The Consultant shall demonstrate experience working on assignments financed by International Financial Institutions (IFIs), and its eligibility including but not limited to meeting the debarment and sanctions standard, financial and commercial capability and fiduciary and system compliance. The Consultant shall have no conflict of interest and pass integrity check.  The attention of interested consultants is drawn to Paragraphs 3.14 to 3.17 of the World Bank's Procurement Regulations for Borrowers, dated July 2016, revised in November 2017, August 2018, November 2020, and September 2023, setting forth the World Bank's Policy on Conflict of Interest.

 

  1. CONSULTANT QUALIFICATIONS EVALUATION CRITERIA

 

  • Overall years of consulting experience (20 points)
  • Number of similar assignments (70 points)
  • Availability of key experts to carry the assignment (10 points)

 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications. Where Consultants propose to associate, the submission shall include evidence of the proposed association from all participating firms.

 

A Bidders workshop will be held virtually to discuss the assignment overview on 21 October 2026. Details will be announced via MME and World Bank platforms. 

 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the CS-CQS method set out in the World Bank's Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, dated July 2016, revised in November 2017, August 2018, November 2020, and September 2023.
