REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES - FIRMS SELECTION)

 

 

Republic of North Macedonia

Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Water Economy

ZLETOVICA PRODUCTIVITY THROUGH IRRIGATION AND RENEWABLE ENERGY PROJECT (PIREP)

Grant No.: TF-D2152

 

Assignment Title: Update of the (i) technical studies and bidding documents for irrigation and hydropower; (ii) economic and financial project assessment (Phases II and III); and (iii) transboundary water analysis

Reference No.: PIREP-CS-QCBS-01

 

The Republic of North Macedonia has received World Bank financing through the Grant Facility for Project Preparation (GFPP) to prepare the Zletovica Productivity through Irrigation and Renewable Energy Project (PIREP), and intends to apply part of the grant proceeds to these consulting services. The Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Water Economy (MAFWE), through its Project Implementation Unit (PIU), implements the preparation grant in partnership with PE HS Zletovica.

The main objective of the consulting services (the “Services”) is to validate and update the available feasibility studies and prepare construction-ready final detailed designs, statutory and permit documentation, and technical components of bidding packages for Phase 2 Irrigation and Phase 3 Hydropower of the Zletovica Hydro-System. Both components shall be prepared concurrently, with equal priority, as an integrated Project.

The Services include review and gap analysis; supplementary surveys and investigations; updated hydrology, water balance, reservoir-operation and climate-resilience analyses; verification of existing Phase 1 assets and HPP B; irrigation and hydropower feasibility assessments; component-level and integrated economic and financial analysis; the OP 7.50 transboundary-waterways technical assessment; jobs and financing-readiness assessments; dam-safety review, remedial measures and instruments; final detailed designs and technical bidding packages; and preparation and submission of applications and follow-up through issuance of the construction permits and prerequisite approvals for both phases.

The Consultant shall coordinate with the separately engaged environmental and social consultant and incorporate accepted requirements into its outputs. The PIU’s independent procurement expert is responsible for the procurement strategy and non-technical procurement documentation. Formal riparian communications and notifications remain the responsibility of the Client, Government and/or the World Bank, as applicable.

The assignment shall be completed within a period of ten (10) months from the Commencement Date, and no later than December 20, 2027, whichever occurs earlier, unless amended in accordance with the Contract. If commencement occurs after 20 February 2027, the Consultant shall submit a compressed, resource-loaded program for the Client’s written approval at inception, in accordance with Section 9 of the Terms of Reference. The program shall preserve preparation of both phases, the full scope and acceptance requirements, and adequate time for technical, statutory and World Bank reviews; neither the scope nor the final completion date shall change automatically.

The indicative staffing inputs are 76 Key Expert person-months and approximately 39 Non-Key Expert person-months, excluding translation, language support, administrative support and additional specialist inputs. The staffing requirements and provisions for a justified alternative staffing approach are set out in Section 7.4 of the TOR.

More details about the assignment are provided in the Terms of Reference, which are issued together with this REoI and form an integral part of it. The complete Terms of Reference may also be obtained from the contact address below.

Note: If approval of the Infrastructure Project remains outstanding when the Request for Proposals (RFP) is prepared, the TOR may be revised following shortlisting to include additional services required to complete or update the urban-planning documentation and obtain such approval. The scope and requirements of these additional services will be specified in the RFP, allowing shortlisted Consultants to address them in their technical proposals and include the corresponding costs in their financial proposals.

MAFWE now invites eligible consulting firms ("Consultants") to express their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants are required to submit information demonstrating that they meet the necessary qualifications and possess the relevant experience to carry out the Services. The shortlisting criteria and the information required to assess the capability and experience of the Consultants are set out below.

  • General Qualifications:
  1. At least ten (10) years of relevant technical, operational, and managerial experience in the planning and design of complex hydropower and irrigation infrastructure.
  2. The Consultant shall have an average annual turnover of at least USD 1,000,000, or its equivalent, over the last three (3) completed financial years preceding the deadline for submission of expressions of interest. As proof of compliance, the Consultant shall provide audited financial statements or verified financial statements showing its annual turnover for each of those years. For a joint venture, this requirement shall be met by the members collectively, by adding their average annual turnovers for the relevant three-year period; each member shall provide its corresponding financial statements.
  3. Demonstrated capacity to address North Macedonian design, licensing, permitting, and regulatory requirements, through appropriately qualified personnel, association with firms with suitable national experience, or other clearly defined arrangements.
  4. A valid license for preparing design documentation for Category I structures (License A), or the relevant recognition of foreign qualifications and licenses, as required under the applicable legislation of North Macedonia. The Consultant shall describe how the applicable licensing requirements will be met before undertaking activities requiring such authorization. Further information on recognition of professional authorizations is available at https://mtc.gov.mk/.
  5. For any urban planning activities included in the assignment, the Consultant shall demonstrate compliance with the applicable national licensing requirements. A foreign legal entity shall undertake such activities under a technical cooperation agreement with a domestic legal entity holding a valid license to perform urban planning activities in the Republic of North Macedonia. The domestic legal entity shall act as the lead entity for those activities and shall be responsible for ensuring that the urban plans and other urban planning outputs prepared through this cooperation comply with the applicable law and implementing regulations. As evidence of compliance, the Consultant shall submit a copy of the domestic legal entity’s valid urban planning license and, where the Consultant is a foreign legal entity, the technical cooperation agreement specifying the parties’ respective roles and responsibilities.
  • Specific Qualifications relevant for the assignment:
  1. Successful completion of at least five (5) comparable contracts during the last ten (10) years. These contracts shall collectively demonstrate experience in feasibility studies, final detailed design, and preparation of bidding documentation for multipurpose water resources systems, irrigation infrastructure, hydropower facilities, dams, and associated works.
  2. Experience in Europe, the Western Balkans, Central Asia, or countries with comparable legal, regulatory, institutional, hydrological, and permitting conditions. Experience in North Macedonia or neighbouring countries shall be considered an advantage.
  3. Experience in assignments financed by international financial institutions, such as the World Bank, EBRD, EIB, ADB, or comparable institutions. Experience with World Bank-financed operations, including procurement, appraisal, dam safety, and preparation of investments for financing, shall be considered an advantage.

The credibility of the above experience shall be demonstrated by a list of relevant assignments. Each reference shall include the assignment title, location and country; the client or contracting entity; a description of the infrastructure and services provided; the contract value and implementation period; the status and date of completion; and the Consultant’s role and scope of services. For assignments undertaken through an association or sub-consultancy, the reference shall identify the Consultant’s share of the services and the activities it directly performed. References shall be supported by client-issued completion certificates or other client confirmations of satisfactory performance.

Key Experts will not be evaluated individually at the shortlisting stage. Instead, the Consultant’s overall capacity, qualifications and relevant experience to mobilize and manage the required team of experts will be assessed. The qualifications, responsibilities and staffing provisions for Key Experts and supporting personnel remain as specified in Sections 7.2–7.5 of the TOR. No technical or financial proposal is requested at this stage.

The Consultant and its associated firms shall disclose any actual or potential conflicts of interest relating to the assignment or the proposed Zletovica investments, in accordance with the applicable Procurement Regulations.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.15, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers”, Seventh Edition, September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest and unfair competitive advantage.

Consultants may associate with other firms in the form of a joint venture or a sub-consultancy to enhance their qualifications. Interested Consultants shall clearly indicate the form and structure of their association, identify all participating firms, and specify their respective roles and responsibilities in the expression of interest. The arrangements shall cover coordination, quality assurance and delivery of the Services.

In the case of a joint venture (JV), all members shall be evaluated jointly against the firm qualification and relevant experience requirements, taking into account the services to be performed by each member. Each member shall individually meet the applicable eligibility requirements and disclose any actual or potential conflict of interest. All members of the JV shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract if the contract is awarded to that JV.

The JV shall identify its lead member and authorized representative and submit either a JV agreement or a letter of intent signed by all proposed members, specifying their intended roles and their commitment to enter into a JV agreement if selected. The requirements concerning design licensing and the domestic entity leading the urban-planning activities shall be met in accordance with the arrangements specified above and in Section 7.1 of the TOR.

Relevant experience shall be assessed on the basis of the services actually performed by the Consultant or the relevant JV member. A contract cited by more than one member of the proposed JV shall be counted only once towards the minimum number of comparable contracts, while each member’s actual contribution shall be assessed. Years of experience shall not be added arithmetically across members.

For the turnover requirement, only the turnover of the Consultant submitting the expression of interest and, where applicable, its JV members shall be counted; the turnover of proposed sub-consultants shall not be included. The qualifications and roles of proposed sub-consultants shall be identified separately and shall not be presented as the Consultant’s own corporate experience. Participation at the proposal stage shall be governed by paragraph 3.19 of the Procurement Regulations and the provisions of the Request for Proposals.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations, through an open international selection process. Shortlisted firms will be invited to submit proposals using the applicable World Bank Request for Proposals - Consulting Services (Non-supervision) Standard Procurement Document.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours from 08:00 to 16:00, Skopje local time, on working days.

Expressions of interest shall be submitted in English and delivered in written form to the address below (in person, by mail or by e-mail) by Wednesday, November 11, 2026, at 15:00 (Skopje local time - CET, UTC+1).

Project ID No. P501017

Assignment Title: selection and employment of #1 Special Contract Management Advisor as individual consultant for the Ethiopia Education Transformation Operation for Learning (ETOL) program.

Reference No.: ET-MOE-577086-CS-INDV

The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia has received financing from the World Bank and other Development Partners toward the cost of ETOL program and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

  1. Objective of the assignment

The objective of the assignment is to provide implementation support the Ministry of Education in the effective and efficient administration, monitoring, and management of contracts under the Education Transformation Operation for Learning (ETOL) Program, ensuring compliance with World Bank procurement regulations, timely delivery of goods, works, and consulting services, proper contract implementation, timely payments, effective resolution of contractual issues, and strengthened contract management capacity of implementing institutions.

  1. Scope of Work and Specific Duties of the Advisor

The successful advisor is expected to advise and support the Ministry of Education in strengthening the implementation, monitoring, and management of contracts under the ETOL Program. The assignment aims to enhance the Ministry’s capacity to ensure efficient procurement processes, timely delivery of goods, works, and services, proper contract administration, and compliance with relevant government rules and World Bank Procurement Regulations. The advisor shall work closely with the Ministry’s Strategic Affaires Executive, procurement Executive and staff and NPCO, suppliers, contractors, consultants, ETOL implementing agencies, and World Bank procurement officers to address implementation challenges, facilitate timely payments and contract settlements, resolve contractual disputes, maintain accurate records and update STEP for IPF component procurement activities, prepare regular progress reports, and strengthen the capacity of implementing institutions in contract management.

  1. Qualifications and Experience Required

Educational Qualification: BA, MA, PhD in Procurement Management, Logistics and Supplies Management, Business Development, Management, MBA, Marketing Management, Contract Management, Engineering or in a related field.

General Experience: Minimum of 12/10/8 years of General Experience for BA/BSc, MA/MSc, and PhD holders, respectively.

 

Adequacy for the assignment:

  • 8 years of work experience in contract administration of goods, works and consulting services in government and donor funded projects. To work at department level is a plus or advantageous.
  • Having minimum of five years’ experience in contract management.
  • Relevant experience in the contract management of works, goods and selection of consultancy services required.
  • Proven familiarity with World Bank procurement procedures including the World Bank standard procurement documents for procurement of works, goods and selection of consultants
  • Relevant experience in government procurement of high- value works, goods, and services
  • Good understanding of sector development programs and proficiency in the World Bank’s Systematic Tracking of Exchanges in Procurement (STEP) system.
  • Strong staff development experience with demonstrable success in building of capacity and facilitating change using participatory methodologies.

Project Name

Indicative Activity / Budget Line

Component 2: Enabling Environment and Regulatory Harmonization - Payment System Oversight and Regulation.

Activity Reference Number (STEP)

FJ-PIFS-577115-CS-INDV

Assignment Title

Payments System Advisor to the Reserve Bank of Fiji (RBF)

Location of role

Suva, Fiji, with remote inputs. The balance of on-site and remote support will be agreed with RBF and PIFS against the implementation schedule.

Implementing Agency on behalf of participating countries

Pacific Islands Forum Secretariat (PIFS)

Primary Counterpart

Reserve Bank of Fiji (RBF)

Duration of Assignment

Approximately six (6) months for the core assignment. Limited follow-up support for participant onboarding may be agreed through 30 June 2027.

Contract Type and Level of Effort

Time-based individual consultant contract. The expected level of effort is up to 120 working days over 6 months. Payments will be based on approved timesheets and eligible reimbursable expenses, rather than fixed-price deliverables.

Agency Description

The Pacific Islands Forum brings the region together to address shared issues and support cooperation. It works through regional governance, shared resources and policy alignment to support economic growth, sustainable development, good governance and security.

Selection Method

Competitive Selection of an independent individual consultant, subject to procurement plan adjustment, justification, conflict-of-interest review, and World Bank no-objection requirements where applicable.

Country Supported

Fiji. The assignment provides country-specific technical assistance under the regional CBR Project.

Overall Project Objective

To enable continuous access to correspondent banking services in the participating Pacific Island Countries.

Project Length

August 2024 to September 30, 2030

Project Background

The Pacific Islands Forum Secretariat (PIFS) has received financing from the World Bank Group's International Development Association (IDA) for the Pacific Strengthening Correspondent Banking Relationships (CBR) Project. The project supports participating Pacific Island Countries to maintain access to correspondent banking services and address payment, regulatory and financial integrity constraints that contribute to de-risking. Component 2 includes support for payment system oversight and regulation.

The Reserve Bank of Fiji (RBF) issued the Fiji QR Code Standard and Guidelines to the payments industry on 30 October 2025. RBF has also issued a directive and implementation timeline requiring payment service providers that currently offer QR payment services, or intends to introduce them, to align with the prescribed standards and guidelines by 30 June 2027.

RBF’s planned implementation includes a cloud-based solution to act as the QR payments Certificate Authority (CA) for participating payment service providers, to be operated by RBF. At the time of its August 2026 feedback, RBF expected the vendor to be appointed by the end of that month, followed by approximately three months of development and implementation. RBF will confirm the procurement status and implementation timetable before the assignment commences.

The CA vendor is responsible for the platform-specific technical work and documentation included in its contract. RBF has requested technical assistance at the overall QR project level, covering implementation leadership, project management guidance, technical advisory support, quality assurance, participant integration, user testing, project documentation and training. The assignment will also support RBF in addressing National Payment System (NPS) configuration requirements for accepting QR payments.

 

Objective of the Assignment

The objective is to support RBF in leading, coordinating and assuring the implementation and operational readiness of the Fiji QR Code Standardisation Project. The consultant will provide project-wide implementation support and technical advice so that participating institutions, payment-system arrangements and operating procedures are prepared for QR payments in line with the Fiji QR Code Standard and Guidelines.

The consultant will work under RBF’s direction and help coordinate the contributions of vendors, participating institutions and RBF teams. RBF will retain responsibility for project decisions and approvals, including approval of system changes and production launch.

 

Scope of Services

The consultant will work with RBF, participating financial institutions and payment service providers, the CA vendor, other relevant technical providers, PIFS and the World Bank. The following six areas cover the overall QR project. Detailed activities and sequencing will be agreed in the inception work plan.

i. Implementation planning governance and coordination

Support RBF in leading the overall QR implementation and coordinating the work of participating institutions and relevant vendors. Review the applicable standards, guidelines and project plans, and prepare a coordinated work plan covering system preparation, participant integration, testing, training and launch. Provide project management guidance, maintain the project schedule and action tracker, and help RBF address risks, dependencies, reporting protocols, and decisions that affect delivery.

ii. Technical review and implementation support

Provide technical advice and project-level quality assurance across the QR payment process, including participant connectivity, interoperability, payment processing, security, resilience and operational responsibilities.   Support RBF in identifying, reviewing and coordinating the NPS configuration changes required to accept QR payments.  Review proposed changes and implementation evidence with the responsible technical teams, and track issues requiring resolution. Review CA-related interfaces and dependencies where these affect the wider QR project and support RBF review CA/PKI operating framework, including certificate renewal, revocation, key rollovers and overall certificate lifecycle management, without duplicating the vendor’s contracted technical work.

iii. Participant integration and testing

Support participant integration planning and coordinate a common approach to integration testing and user acceptance testing. Prepare or consolidate project-level test plans, test cases and readiness criteria; coordinate test activities; review results; and track issues through correction and retesting. Testing should cover QR code generation and validation, interoperability between participants, payment processing through the relevant NPS arrangements, security and recovery. CA-related tests will be coordinated with the vendor’s testing programme.

iv. Operational procedures and project documentation

Prepare or consolidate the procedures, templates and working documents needed to manage the QR project and support scheme operations. These should cover project governance, participant onboarding, testing, risk and issue tracking, operational responsibilities, incident handling, reporting and launch readiness. Review relevant vendor and participant documentation for consistency with the overall implementation plan. Platform-specific manuals and other CA documentation required under the vendor contract will remain the vendor’s responsibility.

v. Capacity building

Provide practical training and knowledge transfer to RBF staff and participating institutions on QR project implementation, participant responsibilities, testing, operational procedures, incident handling, stakeholder engagement, communications, awareness, adoption activities and ongoing oversight. Include project management guidance for the RBF team and practical use of the documents and templates prepared under the assignment. Coordinate training with vendor-provided instruction so that system-specific training and project-wide capacity building complement each other.

vi. Readiness and implementation support

Support RBF in assessing readiness for pilot testing,  and production launch across the QR project, including participant readiness, completion of user testing, NPS configuration, operating procedures and support arrangements. Identify outstanding issues, recommend actions and help coordinate the initial implementation period. Prepare a completion and handover report with remaining actions and arrangements for continued participant onboarding through the industry compliance deadline.

 

Vii. Clearing, settlement, reconciliation, operations and service management  

Provide support in defining transaction routing, clearing and settlement arrangements, liquidity and finality considerations, reconciliation, exception handling, failed transaction, reversals, refunds and dispute handling procedures. Assist RBF develop managment reports covering transaction volume and value, avilability, failure, fraud, complaints, merchant coverage and adoption, Develop dashboards, data standards and compliance monitoring.   

Scope Exclusions

The consultant will provide independent advisory, coordination and quality assurance support. The CA vendor will remain responsible for developing, configuring, documenting and correcting the CA solution and for other outputs required by its contract. Participating institutions and the responsible system operators or technical providers will remain responsible for implementing changes to their own systems, including authorised NPS configuration changes.

This TOR does not assign the consultant responsibility for software development, production-system administration or delivery of the CA vendor’s contractual obligations. Any independent cybersecurity testing or technical audit will require a separately agreed scope and confirmation of the procurement arrangements before commissioning.

Expected Outputs and Reporting Obligations

The consultant will prepare the following working products in line with the agreed implementation schedule. The inception work plan will confirm submission dates, review responsibilities and dependencies on RBF, vendors and participating institutions. The outputs cover the overall QR project and should incorporate or refer to vendor documentation where appropriate.

Expected Output

Content

Indicative Timing

1. Inception Report and Work Plan

Confirmed QR project scope, implementation plan, roles and responsibilities, schedule, dependencies, initial risk register and coordination arrangements.

At inception

2. Technical and Integration Review

Project-level technical review and advice on participant integration, NPS configuration for QR payments, implementation issues, quality assurance and recommended actions.

During implementation; updated as required

3. Testing and Participant Readiness Package

Integration and user acceptance test plans and cases, readiness criteria, issue tracker and summary of test results and corrective actions.

 

Before and during testing

4. Operational Documentation and Training Package

QR project and operating procedures, templates, working guidance, training materials and records of capacity-building activities.

Before launch and handover

5. Implementation Readiness and Completion Report

Readiness assessment before launch; completion and handover record at the end of the core assignment, including outstanding actions and continued participant onboarding.

Before the launch decision and at assignment completion

 

Reporting Obligations

The consultant will report administratively to the Project Coordinator within the PIFS Project Management Unit (PMU) and work with RBF on a day-to-day technical basis. Technical priorities, work planning and expected outputs will be agreed with RBF, PIFS and the World Bank project team. Coordination will include the PIFS Payment Systems Specialist and Fiji Country Coordinator as relevant.

Short monthly activity notes will summarise work undertaken, meetings held, outputs prepared, implementation progress, issues requiring decisions and planned activities. The consultant will maintain a current action tracker covering responsibilities, deadlines, risks and dependencies, and provide additional progress updates during testing and launch preparation as agreed with RBF. Timesheets and payment documentation will be provided as required by the agreed contract.

Technical outputs will be submitted to RBF and PIFS for review and shared with the World Bank where required under project arrangements. The consultant will incorporate consolidated comments and provide final working products in editable formats, together with a completion and handover record.

Monthly progress update report to be provided to RBF by the 5th working day of the new month.

 

Duration, Location and Institutional Arrangements

The core assignment is expected to run for approximately six months, aligned with the overall QR implementation plan and the CA vendor’s implementation timetable. A limited amount of follow-up support may be required for additional participant onboarding before 30 June 2027. The level of effort and any follow-up period will be agreed before contracting, subject to project needs and available budget.

The assignment will combine work in Suva and remote support. The consultant will propose an input schedule that supports implementation coordination, participant testing, training and launch preparation. The number and identity of initial participants and the balance of on-site and remote inputs will be confirmed with RBF and PIFS.

PIFS will contract the consultant through the Pacific Strengthening CBR Project. RBF will act as the primary technical counterpart, designate the relevant staff and facilitate engagement with the CA vendor, participating institutions and other technical providers. RBF will provide access to relevant standards, guidelines, project documentation and technical information, subject to confidentiality requirements. Meeting facilities and workspace may be provided subject to availability.

 

Performance Indicators

Performance will be assessed through the quality and timeliness of the agreed outputs and the consultant’s support to RBF. The assessment will consider whether the implementation plan and action tracker are maintained; technical and NPS configuration issues are documented and escalated; participant testing and readiness are supported by evidence; and procedures, training and handover materials are usable by RBF after the assignment.

The consultant’s performance will be assessed against its agreed responsibilities. Vendor delivery, participant system changes and RBF approval decisions will remain with the responsible parties, with the consultant expected to identify dependencies and report delays or unresolved issues promptly.

 

Confidentiality and Conflict of Interest

The consultant shall comply with PIFS and applicable World Bank requirements on confidentiality, conflicts of interest, anti-corruption and prevention of fraudulent practices. Sensitive RBF, vendor and participant information shall be used only for the assignment and shall not be published or disclosed without prior written consent from PIFS and RBF, and World Bank clearance where required.

The consultant shall disclose any actual or potential conflict of interest before contract signature and throughout the assignment, including relationships with the CA vendor or participating institutions. The consultant must be able to provide independent advice and quality assurance and shall not review its own vendor deliverables. Participation in related downstream procurement shall be subject to applicable conflict-of-interest restrictions.

 

Consultant Qualification Requirements

The assignment requires a consultant or consulting team with experience in payment systems implementation and the ability to coordinate a multi-participant QR project. The lead consultant or Team Leader should meet the experience requirement below, with access to specialist inputs appropriate to the agreed scope.

Area

Qualification / Experience

Lead consultant / Team Leader

At least 10 years of relevant experience in payment systems or digital payments, including prior support to a central bank, payment system operator or financial-sector regulator.

Project management and coordination

Experience leading or coordinating payment-system implementation, managing vendor and participant dependencies, and providing project management guidance and implementation advice.

QR payments and system integration

Experience with QR code payment schemes, interoperability, payment processing and participant integration, including the payment-system configuration requirements for QR payments.

Quality assurance and testing

Experience with system integration testing, user acceptance testing, production readiness, cybersecurity and operational resilience for payment systems.

Documentation and capacity building

Ability to prepare payment-system procedures, technical and project documentation, templates and training materials, and deliver practical capacity building for RBF and participating institutions.

Specialist inputs

Access to payment-system configuration, cybersecurity and testing expertise, and to public key infrastructure (PKI) / Certificate Authority expertise where needed to address QR integration dependencies. These inputs must respect the CA vendor’s contractual responsibilities.

Regional experience

Experience in Fiji, the Pacific or other small and capacity-constrained markets would be an advantage.

 

Selection Method

The selection process will follow the approved procurement plan and applicable PIFS and World Bank requirements. The procurement documents will specify the evaluation approach for the confirmed consulting arrangement and the requirements set out above. The contract will confirm fees, input schedule, travel arrangements, reporting obligations and confidentiality and conflict-of-interest undertakings.

The Government of Bangladesh is implementing the Inclusive Services and Opportunities for Host Communities and Displaced Rohingya Population (ISO) Project with World Bank financing. The Project Development Objective is to improve access to human capital services for vulnerable host communities and displaced Rohingya populations. Component 3, implemented by the Department of Social Services (DSS) under the Ministry of Social Welfare (MoSW), supports social care, child protection, and economic empowerment interventions for the Host Communities and Forcibly Displaced Myanmar Nationals (FDMN) in Chattogram Division. Under this assignment, DSS intends to conduct independent Monitoring, Evaluation, and Operational Reviews (Spot Checks) to assess whether child protection and economic empowerment interventions under the ISO Project are being implemented in accordance with approved guidelines / procedures and agreed protocols. The assignment will verify operational performance, beneficiary targeting, service delivery quality, use of systems among others and assess progress toward intended outputs and outcomes.

Purpose

The Monitoring, Evaluation and Operational Review (Spot Checks) will be conducted in a representative sample of locations where ISO Project interventions are being implemented for both Host Community (Chattogram Division) and FDMN populations (Camps in Cox’s Bazar and Bhasan Char). The assignment will cover both Child Protection and Economic Empowerment interventions. The NGO will be responsible for conducting independent monitoring, evaluation and operational reviews to assess operational performance, beneficiary targeting, use of digital systems, adequacy and capacity of human resources, quality of service delivery Relevant indicators will be drawn from the ISO Project Results Framework, as applicable. The assignment will be implemented over Eighteen (18) months.

Objectives

The objective of this assignment is to conduct independent Monitoring, Evaluation, and Operational Reviews (Spot Checks) to assess whether child protection and economic empowerment interventions under the ISO Project are being implemented in accordance with approved guidelines / procedures and agreed protocols. The assignment will verify operational performance, beneficiary targeting, service delivery quality, use of systems among others and assess progress toward intended outputs and outcomes.

 

The assignment will also involve an outcome evaluation of the social care and economic empowerment interventions in terms of beneficiary households’ progress across a set of relevant socio-economic / welfare indicators. Findings from the operational reviews and outcome evaluation would also need to be analyzed from a gender and social inclusion perspective, identifying any differential experiences or gaps affecting women and vulnerable groups, and will provide practical recommendations to support corrective actions and continuous improvement.

  • At least 10 years of relevant experience in monitoring, evaluation, operational reviews, or spot checks of large-scale development programs, preferably in Bangladesh or the region.

  • Adequate organizational capacity to manage multi location field operations and deploy digitally equipped field teams across multiple districts and camps.
  • Demonstrated experience in monitoring or evaluating child protection, social service workforce, case management, or gender-based violence prevention and response programs.

Request for Expression of Interest 

Country: Kosovo 

Project IDs: P507659 and P507881 

Reference Nr.:  TTFP-CS-IC-3.026 

Project Names: Western Balkans Trade and Transport Facilitation 2.0 (WBTTFP) and Kosovo Financial Sector Development (FinDev) 

  

Position: Monitoring and Evaluation Specialist 

Background 

The Government of Kosovo (GoK), with support from World Bank financing, has established the Central Support Division for Implementing Development Projects (CSD) within the Ministry of Finance (MF). The CSD will serve as a centralized Project Implementation Unit (PIU) for selected development projects where the GoK or independent public institutions are direct beneficiaries.  

The CSD and its PIU will support the implementation of two World Bank-financed projects: the Western Balkans Trade and Transport Facilitation 2.0 Project (P507659) and the Kosovo Financial Sector Development Project (P507881). 

The Western Balkans Trade and Transport Facilitation 2.0 Project is supported through a combination of EUR 12 million grant financing and EUR 34.7 million loan financing. Its objective is to increase trade and transport efficiency and strengthen quality infrastructure in Kosovo and the Western Balkans region. The project will finance improvements at key Border Crossing Points, modernization of customs and border services infrastructure, procurement of equipment, and digitalization of trade-related procedures through systems such as the National Single Window (NSW), the New Computerized Transit System (NCTS), and upgrades to ASYCUDA. It will also support investments to improve market competitiveness, including laboratory equipment for quality testing, an e-tolling system, 5G corridor infrastructure, road safety improvements, and rail safety upgrades at selected railway level crossings. 

The Kosovo Financial Sector Development Project is supported through an EUR 49.3 million loan and aims to improve financial stability and inclusion in Kosovo. The project will support the strengthening of the Deposit Insurance Fund of Kosovo, by providing the capital needed to increase the deposit insurance coverage limit and reduce the payout period for insured depositors following an insured event. It will also expand access to finance for underserved firms through Partial Credit Guarantees via the Kosovo Credit Guarantee Fund, support the development of a National Development Bank, and finance the development of a modern and interoperable Fast Payment System to promote faster and more efficient digital payments. 

Both projects include activities aimed at strengthening project management and implementation capacity, including capacity building for the CSD, PIU staff, and relevant public institutions involved in project implementation. The PIU will be responsible for the day-to-day coordination and implementation of project activities, including fiduciary, technical, monitoring, reporting, and coordination functions, in cooperation with the relevant beneficiary institutions and World Bank task teams. 

Responsibilities of the Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Specialist 

The objective of this consultancy is to establish, operationalize, and maintain a robust, integrated Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) system for TTFP 2.0 and FinDev in Kosovo. The M&E Specialist will ensure systematic tracking, validation, analysis, and reporting of all Project Development Objectives (PDO) indicators, Intermediate Results Indicators (IRIs), Environmental and Social Commitment Plan (ESCP) metrics, and citizen engagement/gender indicators in strict alignment with the Project Results Framework, Project Operations Manual (POM), and World Bank reporting guidelines. 

The M&E Specialist will ensure that project activities for both projects are systematically monitored, evaluated, and reported in alignment with World Bank standards and the project’s results framework. The role will also contribute to strengthening institutional capacity for M&E within the Project Implementation Unit (PIU) and beneficiary agencies, with a particular focus on stakeholder engagement and gender-responsive monitoring. 

Minimum (Mandatory) Qualifications: 

Education: 

  • Master's degree in economics, Public Policy, Statistics, Social Sciences, Business Administration, or related fields. 

Professional Experience: 

  • General Experience: Minimum 8 years of professional experience in monitoring and evaluation of public sector or donor-funded development projects. 

  • Specific M&E Experience: Minimum 8 years of professional experience in monitoring and evaluation of public sector or donor-funded development projects, with experience with projects financed by international financial institutions (ex: World Bank, EBRD, KfW, EIB, etc.) or development agencies (UN, GIZ, etc.) considered as an advantage.  

  • Cross-Cutting Tracking: Proven track record in tracking Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) metrics, Grievance Redress Mechanisms (GM), gender targets, and citizen engagement indicators. 

 

Additional (Desired) qualifications: 

  • Methodological Expertise: Technical knowledge of Time Release Studies (TRS), WCO Data Models, Global Quality Infrastructure Index (GQII) methodologies, or transport sector performance metrics is an advantage. 

  • Fiduciary Systems: Familiarity with World Bank IPF reporting is an advantage. 

  • Advanced proficiency in statistical and data management software (e.g., SPSS, Stata, Power BI, Excel, or R). 

Languages & Technical Skills: 

  • Fluency in Albanian and English is required; English proficiency will be assessed against proof of certificates received (TOEFL, IELTS, etc), and/or documented work experience in an international or English-speaking setting and/or reference to English language proficiency in a reference letter. 

Duration of the Assignment 

Initial 12-month full- time contract, with the possibility of extension for the full projects' duration (3–5 years) subject to satisfactory annual performance evaluation and project requirements. The engagement is expected to continue until the closing dates of the FinDev Project in June 2030 and the WBTTFP Project in December 2031, including any extensions approved by the World Bank. The contract shall include a six-month probationary period. Continuation and renewal shall be subject to satisfactory performance, based on a written evaluation prepared by the Head of PIU and endorsed by the Director of the Department of Financing. 

Application Procedure 

All interested applicants shall submit the following documents: 

  • Curriculum Vitae (CV); 

  • Letter of interest (500 words maximum) 

  • Copies of relevant certificates and diplomas; 

  • At least one (1) and up to three (3) reference letters from previous employers or clients, including official contact details (email and telephone number), or other documentary evidence demonstrating the required experience, such as contract award letters, certificates of completion, employer confirmations, service certificates, or similar references.   

Selection Process 

Experienced and qualified individuals shall be selected in accordance with the provisions of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, dated September 2023, through an open competitive selection process. 

Evaluation Criteria: 

  • General Experience                     (60 Points)

SOLICITUD DE EXPRESIONES DE INTERÉS

SERVICIOS DE CONSULTORÍA

Préstamo nº: BIRF 9624-DO.

Referencia STEP Nº: DO-EDEESTE-571491-CS-QCBS.

El Gobierno de la República Dominicana ha recibido financiamiento del Banco Mundial por un monto de US$225 millones para cubrir el costo del Programa de Mejoramiento de Redes de Media y Baja Tensión y Normalización de Clientes de las Empresas Distribuidoras de Electricidad a Nivel Nacional. La Empresa Distribuidora de Electricidad del Este, S.A. (EDEESTE), a través de la Unidad Ejecutora de Proyectos (UEP), tiene la intención de aplicar parte de los fondos de este financiamiento a la contratación de servicios de consultoría.

Los servicios de consultoría tienen como objetivo brindar apoyo a la Dirección de Proyectos de EDEESTE en la supervisión del Proyecto BIRF 9624-DO, garantizando la ejecución eficiente, segura y controlada de las actividades realizadas por las empresas contratistas y supervisoras, asegurando el cumplimiento de los requisitos contractuales, normativos y de calidad establecidos para el proyecto.

El Proyecto contempla la rehabilitación y modernización de redes de distribución eléctrica, instalación de transformadores, redes de media y baja tensión, sistemas de alumbrado público, acometidas eléctricas, sistemas de medición y normalización de más de 147,000 usuarios ubicados en Santo Domingo Este, Santo Domingo Norte, La Romana y La Altagracia.

La consultoría comprenderá, entre otras actividades:

  • Apoyo a la supervisión de obras de rehabilitación de redes eléctricas de media y baja tensión.
  • Seguimiento y control de la ejecución física de las obras.
  • Validación de cubicaciones y mediciones de avance.
  • Supervisión de la instalación de transformadores de distribución, acometidas, alumbrado público y sistemas de medición.
  • Supervisión de cumplimiento de normas de calidad, seguridad y salud ocupacional.
  • Seguimiento al desempeño de las empresas contratistas y supervisoras.
  • Apoyo en la revisión y control documental de los contratos.
  • Seguimiento al cierre técnico de las obras y elaboración de documentación As-Built.
  • Seguimiento a los requisitos ambientales y sociales del Proyecto, incluidos los instrumentos de gestión ambiental y social aplicables (PGAS, procedimientos de seguridad y demás instrumentos aprobados para el proyecto).

La duración estimada de la consultoría será de treinta (30) meses.

Los Términos de Referencia (TDR) para la presente consultoría podrán consultarse y descargarse en la página web de EDEESTE o solicitarse mediante correo electrónico a la dirección indicada en este aviso.

CRITERIOS PARA LA CONFORMACIÓN DE LA LISTA CORTA

Perfil y Experiencia General de la Firma:

  • Actividad principal relacionada con servicios de consultoría de ingeniería, supervisión de obras, gestión de proyectos o gerencia de construcción.
  • Experiencia general mínima de cinco (5) años en la prestación de servicios de consultoría relacionados con infraestructura eléctrica, supervisión de obras, gestión de proyectos, gerencia de construcción o ingeniería, demostrada mediante contratos ejecutados satisfactoriamente.

Experiencia Específica:

  • Experiencia en al menos tres (3) contratos de supervisión, gerencia, inspección o apoyo a la gestión de proyectos de construcción, rehabilitación o modernización de redes eléctricas de distribución ejecutados durante los últimos diez (10) años.
  • Experiencia en supervisión de proyectos de redes de media tensión, baja tensión, transformadores de distribución, acometidas y sistemas de medición.
  • Experiencia en control de calidad, cubicaciones, seguimiento físico-financiero y administración contractual de obras.
  • Experiencia en supervisión de seguridad industrial, salud ocupacional y cumplimiento ambiental y social en proyectos de infraestructura.
  • Se valorará experiencia en proyectos financiados por organismos multilaterales de desarrollo, incluyendo Banco Mundial, BID, CAF u organismos equivalentes.

Capacidad Técnica y Administrativa:

  • Capacidad demostrada para gestionar simultáneamente múltiples frentes de trabajo.
  • Disponibilidad de sistemas y metodologías de seguimiento y control de proyectos.
  • Estructura organizacional adecuada para administrar contratos de alta complejidad técnica.

La conformación de la lista corta se realizará sobre la base de la experiencia pertinente de las firmas consultoras y de su capacidad técnica, administrativa y organizacional para ejecutar satisfactoriamente los servicios requeridos.

En consecuencia, las firmas consultoras interesadas no deberán presentar hojas de vida, certificaciones ni credenciales del personal propuesto en esta etapa. Dicha información será requerida únicamente a las firmas que resulten incluidas en la lista corta durante la fase de Solicitud de Propuestas (SDP).

  • Carta de expresión de interés firmada por representante autorizado.
  • Perfil institucional de la firma.
  • Evidencia de experiencia general y específica relevante para los servicios requeridos.
  • Para cada experiencia presentada, indicar: cliente, país, objeto del contrato, período de ejecución, monto, alcance de los servicios, rol desempeñado por la firma y evidencia de terminación satisfactoria o aceptación por parte del cliente.

  • Registro Mercantil vigente o documento equivalente emitido en el país de origen.

La información suministrada deberá ser suficiente para demostrar el cumplimiento de los criterios de preselección establecidos. EDEESTE podrá solicitar aclaraciones o documentación complementaria durante el proceso de evaluación de las expresiones de interés.

En caso de APCA, todos los socios serán solidariamente responsables de la ejecución del contrato en caso de resultar seleccionados.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (EOI)

Individual Consultant Selection (INDV)

Ethiopian Statistical Service (ESS)

Project:-Modernizing Ethiopia’s Statistical System Project (MESSP) – Preparation Grant for Modernizing Ethiopia’s Statistical System Project 

Project ID:-P516394 Grant No. E6970-ET 

Assignment Title:- Hiring of a Project Manager for PIU

Reference No.ET-ESS-574077-CS-INDV

1. Background

The Ethiopian Statistical Service (ESS) has received financing from the World Bank and intends to apply part of the proceeds to recruit an individual consultant under the Individual Consultant Selection (INDV) method.

The project aims to improve the availability, quality, timeliness, and use of official statistics for evidence-based policymaking in Ethiopia. ESS will establish a Project Implementation Unit (PIU) responsible for day-to-day implementation, including coordination, procurement, financial management, monitoring and evaluation, environmental and social risk management, reporting, annual work planning and budgeting, procurement planning, and liaison with the World Bank and key stakeholders.

 2. Assignment Objective

The Project Manager will provide overall leadership and management of the PIU to ensure effective, efficient, and compliant implementation of project activities in accordance with the Financing Agreement, Project Implementation Manual, annual work plans, procurement plans, fiduciary requirements, environmental and social commitments, and World Bank procedures.

3. Scope of Services / Duties and Responsibilities

The Project Manager shall, among other duties:

- Provide overall strategic leadership, direction, and management of the project. 

- Coordinate the preparation and implementation of annual work plans, procurement plans, training plans, ICT modernization plans, and project budgets. 

- Ensure timely implementation of project activities in accordance with approved project documents, financing agreements, and implementation schedules. 

- Lead and coordinate digital transformation and ICT modernization initiatives under the project, aligned with ESS strategic priorities and national digital transformation agendas. 

- Coordinate technical, fiduciary, safeguards, monitoring and evaluation (M&E), ICT, and administrative functions of the PIU. 

- Serve as the primary liaison between ESS and key institutions including the Ministry of Finance (MoF), Ministry of Planning and Development (MoPD), sector ministries, development partners, and the World Bank. 

- Ensure compliance with World Bank procurement, financial management, environmental and social safeguards, digital governance, cyber security, and reporting requirements. 

- Supervise consultants, specialists, and support staff recruited under the project, including ICT and digital transformation specialists. 

- Facilitate coordination with sector institutions to strengthen data integration, interoperability, and administrative data systems. 

- Lead the preparation and submission of quarterly, semi-annual, and annual project progress reports. 

- Organize and coordinate Steering Committee and Technical Committee meetings. 

- Monitor project implementation progress and recommend corrective actions where necessary. 

- Identify project risks (including ICT-related risks) and oversee mitigation measures. 

- Ensure stakeholder engagement, communication, and change management activities. 

- Perform any other related duties assigned by ESS management.

4. Duration and Duty Station

Duration:-18 months, full-time, subject to satisfactory performance and project requirements. 

-Duty Station:-ESS Headquarters, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.

The project preparation phase will be up to eighteen (18) months from the date of hiring. Implementation is expected to commence upon Project Effectiveness and continue for approximately five (5) years, with possible overlap between preparation and implementation phases.)

5. Minimum Qualifications and Experience

Education:-

- Master’s degree or above in Statistics, Economics, Information Systems, Computer Science, Public Administration, Project Management, Development Studies, ICT for Development, or related field.

Professional Experience:

- Minimum ten (10) years of relevant professional experience, including at least five (5) years in project coordination/management/program management roles. 

- Demonstrated experience managing large-scale, multi-stakeholder, donor-funded development projects. 

- Proven experience coordinating and implementing World Bank-financed projects is mandatory (experience with other multilateral/bilateral donors is an added advantage). 

- Demonstrated experience in ICT modernization, digital transformation, e-government, statistical modernization, or data system strengthening initiatives. 

- Strong understanding of digital technologies, data ecosystems, information systems, administrative data integration, interoperability frameworks, and digital governance principles. 

- Proven experience working with PIU and managing multidisciplinary teams (procurement, financial management, safeguards, ICT, and M&E). 

- Strong knowledge of World Bank operational policies and procedures including procurement, financial management, safeguards, M&E, and reporting requirements. 

- Experience with national statistical systems and public sector institutions is highly desirable.

6. Selection Method

The consultant will be selected in accordance with the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers – Selection of Individual Consultants (INDV) method.

Interested candidates shall submit an Expression of Interest (EOI) and an updated CV including relevant qualifications and experience, electronically no later than:

Agency Description

The Pacific Islands Forum was established to bring together the region to address pressing issues and challenges, and foster collaboration and cooperation in the pursuit of shared goals. PIF’s mandate is to strengthen cooperation and integration in the Pacific region through the pooling of regional governance, resources and the alignment of policies, furthering Forum members shared goals of economic growth, sustainable development, good governance and security. Founded in 1971, it comprises 18 members: Australia, Cook Islands, Federated States of Micronesia, Fiji, French Polynesia, Kiribati, Nauru, New Caledonia, New Zealand, Niue, Palau, Papua New Guinea, Republic of Marshall Islands, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, and Vanuatu.  The PIFS is a vital platform for Leaders to convene, engage in discussions and agree on policies that will benefit the people of the region.

Participating Countries

The Pacific Island Countries (PICs) participating in the regional project comprise Fiji, Kiribati, the Marshall Islands, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, and Vanuatu

Overall Project Objective

The Project development Objective is to enable continuous access to correspondent banking services in the participating Pacific Island Countries

August 2024 to September 30 2030

 

2. Project Background

The Pacific Island Forum Secretariat (PIFS) is expecting to receive financing from the World Bank (WB) Group’s International Development Association (IDA) for a proposed project to enable continuous access to correspondent banking services in Pacific Island Countries (PICs).  The PICs covered by the proposed regional project (Fiji, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, and Vanuatu) include diverse island economies facing similar correspondent banking relationship challenges.

PICs range in size and topography – from small island states such as Samoa, with two principal inhabited volcanic islands, to large archipelagos such as the Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI), with 29 atolls spread over 2 million km2 of ocean. Population sizes vary from 11,300 people in Tuvalu to 930,000 people in Fiji.

The economic landscape of PICs is equally diverse, marked by different growth drivers, poverty rates, and growth trajectories. The average GDP growth across PICs decelerated to 3.5 percent in 2023 after a historically high of 7.9 percent in 2022, in a rebound from the COVID-19 crisis. However, medium-term growth prospects have worsened, with output growth expected to be significantly below the pre-pandemic trend of 4.7 percent between 2014 & 2019. Given low growth and limited employment opportunities in the island economies, labor migration to neighboring countries and the resulting remittances are critical drivers of living standards.

The United States, New Zealand, and Australia account for 94 percent of the Pacific diaspora. Trade and tourism are vital for many PICs, providing revenue and employment opportunities. Remittances, equivalent to more than 40 percent of GDP in some PICs, are a buffer against income shocks and an important source of finance for essential household consumption and human capital investment.

Financial systems in PICs are characterized by low levels of financial access and an uneven development of national payment systems. Both domestically owned and multinational commercial banks dominate the financial sector in all PICs.  In several PICs, much of the population lacks access to basic transaction accounts, limiting households and businesses’ ability to send and receive payments, save, invest, and respond to climatic and economic shocks. The financial market infrastructure is underdeveloped, in part due to limited competition and the lack of economies of scale. The level of national payment system development is uneven across PICs, and regional efforts to improve the efficiency of cross-border payments are limited in scale and scope.

PICs are uniquely vulnerable to the withdrawal of the correspondent banking relationships (CBR) that underpin international trade, tourism, remittances, and humanitarian financial flows. Correspondent banking is an arrangement under which one bank (correspondent) holds deposits owned by other banks (respondents) and provides payment and other services to those respondent banks. CBRs are an essential feature of the global payment system – they enable individuals, businesses, and governments to make and receive cross-border payment services related to remittances, e-commerce, trade, and official sector flows. The cross-border transactions enabled in PICs are in various currencies, primarily the US dollar, Euro, and Australian dollar.

The withdrawal of CBRs, a well-documented global phenomenon affecting many emerging markets and developing economies, has adverse consequences and negative externalities for Pacific Islanders, including seasonal laborers, small and medium enterprises (SMEs), and vulnerable populations. Based on publicly available data, the number of active correspondents for Pacific banks has declined significantly since 2011 to levels that put the Pacific financial system overall at risk.

In order to mitigate the issues identified above, the WB will provide funding to the Pacific Islands Forum Secretariat (PIFS) to implement the proposed “Pacific Strengthening Correspondent Banking Relationships Project”.  The Pacific Islands Forum was established to bring together the region to address pressing issues and challenges and foster collaboration and cooperation in pursuing shared goals. PIF’s mandate is to strengthen cooperation and integration in the Pacific region through the pooling of regional governance, resources, and the alignment of policies, furthering Forum members' shared goals of economic growth, sustainable development, good governance, and security. Founded in 1971, it comprises 18 members: Australia, Cook Islands, Federated States of Micronesia, Fiji, French Polynesia, Kiribati, Nauru, New Caledonia, New Zealand, Niue, Palau, Papua New Guinea, Republic of Marshall Islands, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, and Vanuatu.    The PIFS is a vital platform for Leaders to convene, engage in discussions, and agree on policies that will benefit the people of the region.

The project will have two components: (1) Temporary correspondent banking services and (2) Enabling environment and regulatory harmonization.  The proposed project will be implemented by a Project Management Unit (PMU) within the PIFS with strategic project oversight provided by a Project Steering Committee (PSC) comprised of representatives of participating Pacific Finance Ministers. While the PMU will be responsible for day-to-day project activities, it will need to ensure close collaboration and coordination with participating Ministries of Finance, which will oversee project activities and approve work plans through the PSC.

Comprising of Secretaries of Finance or other officials from the participating PICs finance ministries and the PIFS Director (Programs and Initiative), the PSC will meet on a quarterly basis and be responsible for the approval of key project activities as needed. The PSC will report to Pacific Finance Ministers annually at the Forum Economic Minister Meeting (FEMM) to ensure that strategic guidance and orientation are provided over the project activities. At the technical level, each participating PIC will be required to nominate a competent   government official as a Country Focal Point (CFP) responsible for project coordination at the national level, who will be designated as the point of contact with the PMU and the WB team.

The competent government official in each PIC will be complemented by a country coordinator (CC) based in-country, recruited through the PMU, and responsible for coordinating service delivery at the individual country level.

The PIFS is now seeking qualified and competent national consultants from each member country to be the country coordinator (CC) for the PMU and based in the respective participating Pacific Island countries (PICs).  The required positions are expected to be selected by the PIFS in accordance with the WB’s ‘Procurement Regulations for Investment Project Financing (IPF) Borrowers’ (Procurement Regulations), fifth edition, September 2023, and as amended over time.

 

3. Objective of the Position

The main objective of the CC would be to manage and coordinate the full range of project, country specific activities during the project cycle from effectiveness through implementation to completion.  The CC will be funded by the project (through the PMU) and report to the PIFS/ PMU Coordinator.  In addition, he/she will work closely with the specific Country Focal Point (CFP), a government official appointed by the MOF of that particular PIC.

The CC will be required to work in a pro-active manner, and to help ensure effective implementation of activities and delivery of outputs in a timely manner.

  11. Work closely with the CFP in preparing annual reports on country specific activities to be submitted to the MOF and PIFS; and
  12. Any other activities as requested by the CFP or the PMU Project Coordinator.

The CC will work closely with the Country Focal Person (CFP) and report to the PMU Project Coordinator.

 

6. Institutional Arrangements

This is a part-time work assignment, with the Consultant expected to be based in in their home country. The Consultant will be supported by the PIFS PMU based in Suva, Fiji but will work closely with and report to the country focal person in the first instance. The CC is expected to show flexibility in working arrangements as time inputs will fluctuate based on country requirements. The work will be part-time averaging approximately 12  days per month for the next six years. A contract will initially be signed for two years with a performance based extension every two years thereafter. Performance evaluation shall be the basis for the extension or termination of the services. Facilities such as office space, intercom telephone facilities, personal computers, printing facilities, Internet access and stationery will be provided.

The following performance indicators shall be used for performance assessment:

  1. Positive progress and good performance of the entrusted project activities, as per the TOR;

The consulting services (“the Services”) aim to engage a highly qualified Technical Lead / Chief Architect to provide independent technical leadership for the Integrated Tax Administration System (ITAS). The role will focus on strengthening enterprise architecture, governing system design, ensuring compliance with approved standards, and overseeing vendor performance in alignment with program objectives and governance frameworks.

The role also includes oversight of vendor activities, management of technical risks, and ensuring compliance with security, scalability, and performance requirements. Given the scale, complexity, and national importance of this program, the Ministry seeks an experienced Chief Architect with a proven track record in large-scale IT system implementations within multi-stakeholder environments.

notice_text:
SOLICITUD A PRESENTAR EXPRESIONES DE INTERÉS

República de Guatemala

 

Proyecto: Finanzas Públicas Inteligentes: Gestión del Gasto Público basada en datos para una mayor eficiencia (P510861).

Convenio BIRF No. 9869-GT

El Gobierno de la República de Guatemala suscribió un Convenio de Préstamo con el Banco Internacional de Reconstrucción y Fomento – BIRF – (Banco Mundial – BM) para financiar el Proyecto "Finanzas Públicas Inteligentes: Gestión del Gasto Público basada en datos para una mayor eficiencia", y se propone utilizar parte de estos fondos para efectuar pagos de los gastos elegibles en virtud del Convenio de Préstamo.

El Proyecto tiene como objetivo mejorar la eficiencia, la eficacia y la rendición de cuentas del gasto público de la República de Guatemala, mediante el fortalecimiento de los procesos y metodologías de presupuesto, inversión pública, deuda, tesorería, contabilidad y transparencia fiscal". En este contexto, el fortalecimiento de los procesos y metodologías de presupuesto, inversión pública, deuda, tesorería, contabilidad y transparencia fiscal constituye un elemento clave para una gestión del gasto más eficiente y orientada a resultados.

El Ministerio de Finanzas Públicas, a través de la Unidad Ejecutora “Modernización de las Finanzas Públicas”, invita a consultores individuales elegibles a expresar su interés en prestar los servicios de consultoría solicitados. Los consultores interesados deberán proporcionar Carta de Interés y Hoja de Vida (CV) con información que indique están cualificados para suministrar los servicios.

2. The objective of the consultancy assignment is to support the entire Transport Portfolio and all Project Implementation Units (PIUs), to strengthen the PIU's technical capacity in order to guarantee the adequate implementation of the all activities related to the project. Therefore, the consultant will be responsible for implementing and supervising the activities in specific areas of the CRRN following ANE guidelines, manuals and standards.

3. The detailed Terms of Reference (ToR) for the assignment can be obtained from the following link: https://www.fe.gov.mz/storage/app/uploads/public/6ac/f15/d5d/6acf15d5d310b271732802.pdf, or alternatively at the address below.

6. The evaluation of expressions of interest will be made on qualitative basis according to a robust matrix of strengths and weaknesses and the shortlist will be composed from the list of qualified individual consultants considering the following criteria:

  1. He/She must have a MSC. Degree in civil engineering, water resources engineering, or a related field with specialization in hydrology or hydraulics.

  7. He/She must have Fluency in written and spoken English is required.

REPUBLIC OF MOZAMBIQUE

MINISTRY OF PUBLIC WORKS, HOUSING AND WATER RESOURCES

URBAN WATER SECURITY PROGRAM – P509890

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST Nº. FIPAAS/UWSP/CON-02/26

 

CONSULTING SERVICES FOR DETAILED ENGINEERING DESIGN, SUPERVISION AND ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL INSTRUMENTS FOR WATER SUPPLY AND SANITATION INFRASTRUCTURE FOR VILANKULO, PAMBARRA AND MAPINHANE

 

1.     The Government of Mozambique, through the Ministry of Public Works, Housing and Water Resources (MOPHRH), has received financing from the World Bank under the Urban Water Security Program (P509890), to be implemented in the Greater Maputo Metropolitan Area and the Southern Region, and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the contract FIPAG/UWSP/CON-02/26 – Consulting Services for Detailed Engineering Design, Supervision and Environmental And Social Instruments for Water Supply and Sanitation Infrastructure for Vilankulo, Pambarra and Mapinhane.

 

2 .     The services include: (i) review of the 2021 studies and detailed engineering design of the water supply infrastructure, the Faecal Sludge Treatment Plant and public sanitation blocks in Vilankulo, Mapinhane and Pambarra; (ii) preparation of the environmental and social instruments and tender documents; and (iii) construction supervision. The expected duration is 10 months for the detailed design (Lump-Sum) and 28 months for construction supervision, including a 12-month Defects Liability Period.

3.       The Water Supply and Sanitation Investment and Assets Fund (FIPAAS) invites eligible firms (“Consultants”) to express their interest in providing the services. Interested Consultants must provide valid information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services (brochures, description of similar assignments, experience in similar conditions, etc.).

 

4.      Attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers”, 7th Edition, September 2025, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

 

5.     The firms are also drawn to paragraph 3.32, of the Section III, related to prohibited practices (fraud, corruption, collusion, coercion, and obstruction) and the Consultants found to have engaged in such practices will be declared ineligible for World Bankfinanced contracts.

 

6.     Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a subconsultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

 

7.      The Consultant shall be a Civil Engineering consulting firm with: (i) - A minimum of 15 (fifteen) years of general experience in the water and sanitation sector; (ii) - At least 10 (ten) years of specific experience in Sub-Saharan Africa; (iii) - have successfully executed at least three (3) projects of hydraulic infrastructure, with similar nature, which may include, but are not limited to: (a) Water supply systems; (b) Sanitation infrastructure; (c) Hydraulic infrastructure for water resources management; (d) Irrigation and (e) productive water use schemes, (iv) - demonstrate experience in assignments implemented under FIDIC Conditions of Contract and/or projects financed by international financing institutions or other internationally financed development programmes, (v) - demonstrate experience with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF), (vi) - World Bank procurement requirements, or equivalent environmental, social and procurement frameworks applied by other international financing institutions, (vii) – have at least six (6) water supply system projects in Sub-Saharan Africa, each including: (a) Surface water abstraction and intake works; (b) Conventional water treatment plants; (c) Reinforced concrete reservoirs with a minimum storage capacity of ≥ 5,000 m³;  (d) Distribution networks with pipe diameters of ≥ 500 mm and (viii) – have at least three (3) detailed engineering designs of sanitation infrastructure, including faecal sludge treatment plants (FSTPs) and associated facilities.

 

8.      Detailed Terms of Reference (ToR) for this assignment may be obtained through the link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1e02RqSChZh-U15BOHDF21QtQQlQmo0r_/view?usp=drivesdk

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

Georgia

Anaklia Rail Hinterland Connectivity Project

Assignment Title: Supervision of Design and Build of a Railway and Related Infrastructure Connecting to the Anaklia Deep-Sea Port

Reference No. GE-GR-577262-CS-QCBS

The Government of Georgia intends to apply for financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the Project, and JSC Georgian Railway intends to utilize part of the proceeds towards payments under the contract for “Design and Build of a Railway and Related Infrastructure Connecting to the Anaklia Deep-Sea Port”, as well as for consulting services (the Services).

 

The Services include “Supervision of Design and Build of a Railway and Related Infrastructure Connecting to the Anaklia Deep-Sea Port”. The Project envisages design and construction of a railway line with its supporting infrastructure, electrification, construction of overpasses and underpasses, drainage channels and pipes, construction of a new railway station “Anaklia”, construction of Khamiskuri junction, reconstruction of existing railway station “Khobi” and construction of service facilities. The Project territory is located between the village Khamiskuri and the Black Sea from East to West direction. From North it is bordered by the rivers Jumi and Enguri, from South – by the villages of Khobi municipality: Tsvane, Mogiri and Torsa. Eastern (about 4km) and Western (about 9km) parts of the territory are uninhabited. Its middle part (about 4km) is populated (the villages: Ergeta, Didi Nedzi and Orulu). The railway line starts at Khamiskuri and ends near the Port area in Anaklia. The total length of the line is approximately 17.74km.

 

The primary objectives of the Consulting Services are as follows: (i) review the Contractor’s detailed design and verify its compliance with the Employer’s Requirements; (ii) function as the Engineer in administering the works contract and execution of all rights and responsibilities of the Engineer in accordance with the “Conditions of Contract for Plant & Design-Build for Electrical & Mechanical Plant & for Building & Engineering Works Designed by the Contractor (“Yellow book”) Second edition 2017, reprinted 2022 with amendments”; (iii) comprehensive supervision of design activities and works carried out by the Contractor to ensure compliance with the drawings, technical specifications and various stipulations contained in the contract documents, with high standards of quality assurance in supervision and in the execution of works; (iv) advise the Client on all matters concerning the contract management and support the Client to have the works completed within the stipulated time for completion and budget.

 

The Consultant is expected to provide 369 person-months (full-time field presence) of consulting services. The Services will be provided over a period of 48 months (including 30 months of design and construction supervision and 18 months of Defects Notification Period).

Digital RMI Project
